More than likely, one person or department won’t have all of the information related to many business functions. For example, sales personnel may not know what quality tests a product goes through. Similarly, the production department won’t necessarily care about the selling price of the product because it’s primarily concerned with or focused on producing it. However, salespeople need instant access to the selling price and the applicable taxes or discounts upon creation of a sales order. Similarly, the pro- duction supervisor wants better control over the underdelivery and overdelivery toler- ances allowed for a material, whereas the warehouse in charge needs instant informa- tion about storing the product. To add greater visibility to the entire material master creation process, the SAP S/4HANA system provides views in which the relevant departments of the company (depending on which SAP S/4HANA functionality they’re working with) can fill in their share of information. The Basic Data view contains basic information that is applicable to the entire material master, such as base units of measure, gross and net weights, vol- ume, product hierarchy, and design/drawing information. We cover the details of these views later in this section. When you’re creating a material master, it’s also important to define the material type—that is, whether it’s a raw material, a semifinished product, a trading good, a spare part, or a consumable item. The material type controls the views that the system makes available for the user to maintain information for later use. The views contain either organization-independent or organization-dependent details. The organization- independent information includes, for example, the material description or its weight and volume. The organization-dependent information—that is, information specific © 197 6.2 Master Data to a plant or storage location—may include the planning or forecasting data that is unique to a given plant. For a different plant (organization dependent), the planning or forecasting data may be different. Table 6.1 provides an overview of plant-independent and plant-dependent views of the material master. A checkmark in a column denotes the data that needs to be main- tained for a given function. The following list provides broad explanations of the data in some of the views of the material master: Material View Organization- Independent Plant Storage Location Storage Number SAP S/4HANA Sales Basic Data 1 and 2  Classification  Sales: Sales Org.   Sales: General/Plant   Foreign Trade/Export Data   Sales Text   Purchasing  Foreign Trade/Import Data  Purchase Order Text  MRP 1–4  Advanced Planning  Forecast   Work Scheduling  Plant Data/Storage 1 and 2    Warehouse Manage- ment 1 and 2   Quality Management  Accounting 1 and 2  Costing 1 and 2  Table 6.1 Material Master Views 6 Production Planning for Discrete Manufacturing 198  Basic data These views consist of information such as base unit of measure, which is the small- est unit of measure in which a company maintains the product’s inventory. It con- sists of gross weight, net weight, volume, product hierarchy, size/dimension, and design/drawing details if you’re using the SAP Document Management service.  Classification This view enables classifying specific materials with identical or similar characteris- tics into groups and categorizing those groups based on specific characteristics. Due to this view’s diverse and practical nature, it’s available in several areas of the SAP S/4HANA system. You can classify materials as well as customers and equipment. When there isn’t any other option to do so, you can use classification to maintain material-specific information.  Sales These views contain details such as the delivering plant, selling unit of measure, taxes, conditions (e.g., gross price, taxes), sales order text, transportation group, loading group, and item category. These views are maintained for materials that a company wants to sell.  Purchasing This view contains the purchase unit of measure, purchase group, material group that groups together materials with similar attributes, purchasing value key that incorpo- rates underdelivery and overdelivery tolerances, GR processing time, and batch man- agement. For externally procured materials, maintaining this view is mandatory.  MRP These views enable a materials planner to define how to procure a material and how to plan and control the material within the production process. The definition of the procurement type specifies whether a company procures the material externally, produces it in house, or can do both. It enables specifying whether the material fol- lows reorder point planning or is demand driven. Using a strategy group, you can maintain controls for whether a material uses make-to-stock (MTS), make-to-order (MTO), or assemble-to-order (ATO) production. Material planning for a procured or produced material requires you to maintain some or all of the MRP views. Note Chapter 13 covers MRP.  Advanced planning Production planning and detailed scheduling (PP/DS) with SAP S/4HANA introduces the advanced capacity planning and heuristics for materials planning that were pre- viously available in SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization (SAP APO). PP/DS transactions are executed directly in SAP S/4HANA, thereby eliminating the need for a separate installation to run PP/DS transactions. The material master and work center creation are also synchronous, which means that a material or a work center that has just been created can be immediately available for planning in PP/DS. © 199 6.2 Master Data  Forecast This view enables a materials planner to define forecasting parameters and models, such as constant, seasonal, moving average, and trend. If you already know the fore- casting data properties, then you can select from one of the available forecasting models. If you don’t know which model to select, the system provides an option for automatic model selection. It requires you to define the number of historical and forecast periods, based on which the system runs forecasting. Note Chapter 11, Section 11.4 covers forecasting.  Work scheduling This view contains details for underdelivery and overdelivery tolerances for in- house production, the production scheduler, the production scheduling profile that controls several business functions, the production unit of measure, and the pro- duction time in days. For material produced in house, maintaining this view is man- datory. It’s possible to have a different unit of measure, which in this case is the pro- duction unit of measure and may be different from the base unit of measure.  Plant data This view contains information such as the storage bin, temperature conditions, and shelf life data for batch-managed materials, including maximum storage period, minimum remaining shelf life, and total shelf life.  Quality management This view provides the option to select different types of inspections that a material may go through—for example, finished goods inspection, raw material inspection, and in-process (during production) inspection. The QM procurement key denotes whether raw material must be quality managed and also denotes the relevant certif- icate type.  Accounting These views contain the price control indicator—that is, whether the material will be valued at a standard price or a moving average price—and the valuation class.  Costing These views contain details such as overhead group, origin group, and variance key. Note The creation of material types and also the material master is largely driven by MM processes, with other functional areas supporting and facilitating it. Now, let’s create a new material and maintain some of the important views. To create a new material master, you follow menu path Logistics  Production  Material Master  6 Production Planning for Discrete Manufacturing 200 Create (General)  Immediately or use Transaction MM01. On the initial screen that appears, select M Mechanical Engineering as the Industry sector and FERT Finished Product from the dropdown list (not shown) as the Material Type. Then, choose Org. (organizational) Levels from the top menu bar so that Figure 6.2 appears. Figure 6.2 Initial Screen for Material Master Creation Next, click Select View(s) and the screen shown in Figure 6.3 will appear, showing the list of views that were briefly covered earlier. Figure 6.3 Selecting View Options in Material Master Creation © 201 6.2 Master Data You don’t need to select and maintain all the views, just those that will eventually be used in your company’s business processes. For example, if material planning is not required, then there’s no need to maintain MRP views of the material. Select the Basic Data views and the screen shown in Figure 6.4 will appear, showing the Basic Data 1 tab of the material master. Here, the system automatically assigns it an internal material number, FG129. In this view, you maintain information such as Base Unit of Measure, Gross Weight, and Net Weight. The right-hand side of the screen shows the various views that can be maintained for this material. Figure 6.4 Basic Data View of Material Master

אב חומר (Material Master) הוא כל מה שהחברה רוצה לתחזק כפריט מלאי — מוצר גמור המיוצר ונמכר, חומר גלם נרכש ונצרך, מתכלים (גריז, חומרי סיכה, כפפות), סחורות מסחר, וחלקי חילוף לתחזוקה. תחזוקת אב החומר היא אחריות משותפת של מחלקות שונות — כל אחת תורמת את חלקה. תחזוקת מידע מובנה לוגית מסייעת למחלקות לבצע את תפקידיהן ביעילות.
בעת יצירת אב חומר, חשוב להגדיר את סוג החומר — גלם, חצי-גמור, סחורת מסחר, חלק חילוף או מתכלה. סוג החומר שולט בתצוגות שהמערכת מנגישה. התצוגות מכילות פרטים עצמאיי-ארגון (תיאור, משקל, נפח) או תלויי-ארגון (ספציפיים למפעל/מיקום אחסון — נתוני תכנון/חיזוי הייחודיים למפעל).

טבלה 6.1 — תצוגות אב החומר (תצוגה | עצמאי-ארגון | מפעל | מיקום אחסון | מספר אחסון | SAP S/4HANA Sales):

הסבר תצוגות נבחרות:
• **Basic data:** יחידת מידה בסיסית (הקטנה ביותר לתחזוקת מלאי), משקל ברוטו/נטו, נפח, היררכיית מוצר, גודל/ממד, ופרטי עיצוב/שרטוט (SAP Document Management).
• **Classification:** סיווג חומרים בעלי מאפיינים זהים/דומים לקבוצות. זמין בתחומים רבים (חומרים, לקוחות, ציוד). משמש כשאין אפשרות אחרת לתחזוקת מידע.
• **Sales:** מפעל מספק, יחידת מכירה, מסים, תנאים (מחיר ברוטו, מסים), טקסט הזמנת מכירה, קבוצת הובלה/העמסה, קטגוריית פריט. לחומרים נמכרים.
• **Purchasing:** יחידת רכש, קבוצת רכש, קבוצת חומרים, מפתח ערך רכש (כולל סבילות תת/עודף-משלוח), זמן עיבוד GR, ניהול אצוות. חובה לחומרים חיצוניים.
• **MRP:** מגדיר כיצד לרכוש ולתכנן חומר. סוג הרכש (procurement type) קובע אם רכש חיצוני, ייצור פנימי, או שניהם; אם מבוסס נקודת הזמנה מחדש או מבוסס-ביקוש; וקבוצת אסטרטגיה (strategy group) לבקרה MTS/MTO/ATO. (פרק 13 — MRP.)
• **Advanced planning:** PP/DS מציג תכנון קיבולת מתקדם והיוריסטיקות (לשעבר ב-SAP APO), המבוצעים ישירות ב-SAP S/4HANA. יצירת אב החומר ומרכז העבודה סינכרונית — זמינים מיד לתכנון ב-PP/DS.
• **Forecast:** פרמטרי ומודלי חיזוי (קבוע, עונתי, ממוצע נע, מגמה), או בחירת מודל אוטומטית. דורש הגדרת מספר תקופות היסטוריות וחזויות. (פרק 11.4 — חיזוי.)
• **Work scheduling:** סבילות תת/עודף-משלוח לייצור פנימי, מתזמן ייצור, פרופיל תזמון ייצור, יחידת ייצור, זמן ייצור בימים. חובה לחומר מיוצר פנימית.
• **Plant data:** תא אחסון, תנאי טמפרטורה, נתוני חיי מדף לחומרים מנוהלי-אצווה.
• **Quality management:** סוגי בדיקה (מוצר גמור, גלם, בתהליך), מפתח רכש QM, סוג תעודה.
• **Accounting:** מחוון בקרת מחיר (תקן או ממוצע נע), מחלקת הערכה (valuation class).
• **Costing:** קבוצת תקורה, קבוצת מקור, מפתח סטייה.
ליצירת אב חומר: Logistics • Production • Material Master • Create (General) • Immediately, או Transaction MM01. במסך ההתחלתי בחרו M Mechanical Engineering כ-Industry sector ו-FERT Finished Product כ-Material Type, ואז Org. Levels (Figure 6.2). לחצו Select View(s) (Figure 6.3) — אין צורך בכל התצוגות, רק הנדרשות. בחרו Basic Data (Figure 6.4) — המערכת מקצה מספר פנימי FG129; מתחזקים Base Unit of Measure, ‏Gross/Net Weight.

**הערת יועץ:** אב-החומר הוא נתון-האב הרוחבי-ביותר ב-SAP, וסוג-החומר (material type) הוא ההחלטה-הקריטית שכן הוא שולט באילו-תצוגות זמינות. מנקודת-מבט-אינטגרטיבית, כל-תצוגה שייכת-למחלקה-אחרת — Basic Data לכולם, MRP ל-PP, Accounting ל-CO/FI, Sales ל-SD — ולכן תחזוקת-אב-החומר היא מאמץ-חוצה-ארגון. יועץ מנוסה מגדיר מטריצת-אחריות (מי-מתחזק-איזו-תצוגה) ומקים תהליך material-master-governance, שכן שדה-שגוי בתצוגת-MRP או Accounting מתגלגל לכשלי-תכנון-ולעיוותי-עלות בכל-מחזור-הייצור.

sections.title: Bill of Materials
sections.en: 6.2.2 Bill of Materials A material’s BOM consists of components grouped together with the relevant quanti- ties that are needed to produce the material in the production process. For example, if vanilla ice cream is the main product, then its BOM will consist of all the ingredients (components) needed to produce it. Similarly, to produce an automobile, there’s a need for an engine, a chassis, a body, and a large number of other components. To create the BOM of a material, follow menu path Logistics  Production  Master Data  Bills of Material  Bill of Material  Material BOM  Create or use Transaction CS01. On the initial screen, enter “FG129” for Material and “1710” for Plant, as shown in Figure 6.5. This is the material number for which you want to create the BOM. In the BOM Usage field, enter “1” to specify the purpose for which you’re creating and using a BOM. BOM 6 Production Planning for Discrete Manufacturing 202 Usage 1 denotes that it’s for production purposes and will be available when creating a production order for this material. Other BOM usages are SD BOM, PM BOM, and Cost- ing BOM. In the Valid From field, enter “01/01/2026” to denote the date from which the BOM becomes available in the production process. In this example, the BOM’s validity starts on January 01, 2026 (01/01/2026), when a user creates a production order. Therefore, the BOM won’t be available if the user creates a production order in the month of December 2025. If no date is given, the system automatically assigns the BOM’s cre- ation date as the Valid From date. The purpose of BOM validity is to ensure that if the company has a new BOM starting at a later date, then the validity of the new BOM can be set accordingly and will become available during the production process. In the Alternative BOM field, you can specify up to 99 different alternative BOMs for a material. This means that the same material can be produced in up to 99 different ways by having an alternative BOM option available. For example, when one component of a material’s BOM is unavailable in stock, a production planner can select another alter- native BOM to continue the production process. When a material’s BOM is created for the first time, the system automatically assigns the alternative BOM as 1. When a new BOM for the same material is created, then the system issues a warning message and internally assigns the next alternative BOM number to it. You choose Header to open the Create Material BOM: Header Overview screen. The base quantity of a material denotes the quantity based on which the material’s BOM components are defined. The system then automatically divides the component’s quantity by the base quantity during production order creation. This is especially use- ful when component quantities are very small and defined in, for example, milligrams, as with vanilla flavor. For this example, you assign a base quantity of “10 PC” in the BOM header as shown in Figure 6.5. The components and their quantities that you define in the BOM now denote the requirements to produce ten pieces of material FG129. The BOM Status field controls whether the BOM is active and is available for usage, and the value 1 denotes that it’s active. If there’s a business need to deactivate a BOM, then you can simply change the status of the BOM to Inactive at any time. Next, click the Item button to go to the screen shown in Figure 6.6, which shows the item overview of the BOM. Enter the material numbers for the individual components, together with the quantity for each. The system will divide the component’s quantity by the base quantity (if any) during production order creation to calculate the quantity of the component needed to produce the main material, which in this case is FG129. © 203 6.2 Master Data Figure 6.5 BOM Header Figure 6.6 BOM Item Overview Select line item 0010 and then choose Item, which opens the screen shown in Figure 6.7. Some of the important fields on this screen are as follows:  Fixed Quantity If you check this box, you’re denoting that regardless of production order quantity, the component quantity remains fixed. For example, to produce 50 kg of a main 6 Production Planning for Discrete Manufacturing 204 material, the component quantity required is 50 kg. To produce 35 kg of the main material, the system calculates the component quantity of 35 kg, as defined in the material’s BOM. However, if you check the Fixed Quantity box and select a compo- nent Quantity of, say, 35 kg, then the system will calculate the component quantity required as 35 kg, even if the main material’s production quantity is 50 kg.  Operation scrap in % Operation scrap is defined as a percentage increases the issuance quantity of a com- ponent to account for scrap during the production process. For example, if you define Operation scrap as 5% and the component quantity as 100 kg, then the sys- tem automatically calculates the required component quantity as 105 kg to account for the operation (during production) scrap. It’s mandatory to select Net ID (not shown) when defining operation scrap.  Component scrap (%) Component scrap is defined as a percentage increase of the issuance quantity of a component to account for scrap during the production process. For example, if you define Component Scrap as 10% and the component Quantity as 100 kg, then the system automatically calculates the required component quantity as 110 kg to account for the operation scrap. Figure 6.7 Detailed View of BOM Item If you define and select both scrap types (operation scrap and component scrap), the system will consider both scrap types during component quantity calculation. During the MRP run, the system will take all of these scrap definitions into account to suggest planning proposals. Next, scroll down the screen (see Figure 6.8). If the normal production of a product gen- erates a coproduct, then you should check the Co-product box. © 205 6.2 Master Data If the production process in a business scenario entails that the main material can also be one of the process’s BOM components, then this will only be possible if you check the Recurs. (recursive) allowed box. Figure 6.8 Additional Details in BOM Item In the MRP Data area of the screen, the Lead-time offset field helps you plan a compo- nent’s availability. For example, if a production supervisor wants to start producing a material as soon as the first shift starts on a given morning, then they will need to approach the warehouse supervisor on the day before to issue the requisite compo- nents. To handle this scenario, you enter “–1” in the Lead-time offset field so that the component’s required availability date is one day earlier than the planned start date of the production. The negative number of the workday reflects that the production supervisor needs components earlier than the start date of production, and a positive number of days is used to show that there’s no need to have the components until the defined number of days after the start of production. The system ignores this option if the production process follows lead-time scheduling (and not just basic date schedul- ing). To enable this behavior for lead-time scheduling, you assign the components to the corresponding operations in the routing. Note that such a positive or negative lead time is always independent of lot size. The Special Procurement field enables a materials planner to define a component- specific special procurement, like a phantom assembly or a procurement from another plant. Maintaining a special procurement type at the component level gives it a higher precedence than at the material level. During an MRP run, the system explodes the material BOM and evaluates parameters maintained at the component level for plan- ning purposes before it looks for the information at the material level. Next, choose the Status/Long Text tab shown in Figure 6.7 to see the fields in Figure 6.9. Enter the Storage Location. During the backflush process in SFC, the system looks for information in this field because it acts as an issue storage location. If the customer or vendor supplies the material instead of the company using its own material in produc- tion, then you should select the relevant option from the Mat. Provision Ind. dropdown list. Finally, you can also control whether the component is considered during product 6 Production Planning for Discrete Manufacturing 206 cost calculation or whether the system excludes it. You do this by selecting the relevant option in the CostingRelevncy field. Figure 6.9 Status/Long Text Tab of BOM Item Details Tips and Tricks You can make mass changes to BOMs to attend to any new business requirements. For example, a materials planner might want to replace an old and obsolete component number in all of the material BOMs in which it’s currently in use or change the compo- nent’s quantity in all of the material BOMs in which it’s in use. For such business sce- narios, you use Transaction CS20 to make mass changes to the BOM. In the upper half of the screen, you define the selection criteria; in the lower half, you define the changes that need to be made. When making the desired changes, be sure to select one of the many radio buttons that are available.
sections.he:
BOM של חומר מורכב מרכיבים וכמויות הנדרשים לייצורו. למשל, גלידת וניל — ה-BOM כולל את כל המרכיבים; לרכב — מנוע, שלדה, מרכב ורכיבים רבים.
ליצירה: Logistics • Production • Master Data • Bills of Material • Bill of Material • Material BOM • Create, או Transaction CS01. במסך ההתחלתי הזינו "FG129" ל-Material ו-"1710" ל-Plant (Figure 6.5). בשדה BOM Usage הזינו "1" — לייצור (זמין ביצירת הזמנת ייצור). שימושים אחרים: SD BOM, ‏PM BOM, ‏Costing BOM.
בשדה Valid From הזינו "01/01/2026" — התאריך שממנו ה-BOM זמין. אם לא ניתן תאריך, המערכת מקצה את תאריך היצירה. תוקף ה-BOM מבטיח ש-BOM חדש המתחיל מאוחר יותר יהיה זמין בהתאם.
בשדה Alternative BOM ניתן לציין עד 99 BOMים חלופיים — אותו חומר ניתן לייצור עד 99 דרכים. למשל, כשרכיב חסר במלאי, המתכנן בוחר BOM חלופי. ביצירה ראשונה, המערכת מקצה alternative BOM 1; ב-BOM חדש לאותו חומר, מנפיקה אזהרה ומקצה את המספר הבא.
בחרו Header. כמות הבסיס (base quantity) קובעת את הכמות שלפיה מוגדרים הרכיבים. המערכת מחלקת את כמות הרכיב בכמות הבסיס ביצירת ההזמנה — שימושי כשכמויות הרכיבים קטנות מאוד (למשל מיליגרמים של טעם וניל). בדוגמה, הקצו base quantity "10 PC" בכותרת — הרכיבים מציינים את הדרישות לייצור עשרה יחידות של FG129.
שדה BOM Status שולט אם ה-BOM פעיל וזמין; הערך 1 = פעיל. ניתן לשנות ל-Inactive בכל עת.
לחצו Item (Figure 6.6) — סקירת פריטי ה-BOM. הזינו מספרי חומר לרכיבים וכמויות. בחרו פריט 0010 ואז Item (Figure 6.7). שדות חשובים:
• **Fixed Quantity:** סימון = כמות הרכיב קבועה ללא תלות בכמות ההזמנה. למשל, אם סומן וכמות הרכיב 35 ק"ג, המערכת תחשב 35 ק"ג גם אם כמות הייצור 50 ק"ג.
• **Operation scrap in %:** מגדיל את כמות ההנפקה של רכיב לחישוב פסולת בתהליך. למשל, 5% וכמות 100 ק"ג → 105 ק"ג. חובה לבחור Net ID בהגדרת פסולת פעולה.
• **Component scrap (%):** מגדיל את כמות ההנפקה לחישוב פסולת. למשל, 10% וכמות 100 ק"ג → 110 ק"ג.
אם מוגדרים שני סוגי הפסולת, המערכת שוקלת את שניהם בחישוב. בריצת MRP, המערכת לוקחת בחשבון את כל הגדרות הפסולת.
גללו (Figure 6.8). אם הייצור מייצר מוצר לוואי, סמנו Co-product. אם החומר הראשי יכול להיות גם רכיב ב-BOM של התהליך, אפשרי רק בסימון Recurs. (recursive) allowed.
באזור MRP Data, שדה Lead-time offset מסייע בתכנון זמינות רכיב. למשל, להתחלת ייצור בבוקר, יש לקבל רכיבים יום קודם — הזינו "–1" כך שתאריך הזמינות הנדרש מוקדם ביום מתאריך ההתחלה. מספר שלילי = רכיבים נדרשים מוקדם; חיובי = אין צורך עד מספר ימים לאחר ההתחלה. המערכת מתעלמת מאפשרות זו בתזמון lead-time (להתנהגות זו, הקצו רכיבים לפעולות במסלול). זמן זה עצמאי מגודל אצווה.
שדה Special Procurement מגדיר רכש מיוחד ספציפי-רכיב (מכלול פנטום, רכש ממפעל אחר). תחזוקה ברמת הרכיב גוברת על רמת החומר. בריצת MRP, המערכת מפוצצת את ה-BOM ומעריכה פרמטרי רמת רכיב לפני רמת חומר.
בחרו לשונית Status/Long Text (Figure 6.9). הזינו Storage Location — בתהליך ה-backflush ב-SFC, המערכת מחפשת כאן (מיקום אחסון להנפקה). אם הלקוח/ספק מספק את החומר, בחרו ב-Mat. Provision Ind. ניתן לשלוט אם הרכיב נשקל בחישוב עלות המוצר בשדה CostingRelevncy.
**Tips and Tricks:** ניתן לבצע שינויים המוניים ל-BOMים — למשל החלפת רכיב מיושן בכל ה-BOMים או שינוי כמות. השתמשו ב-Transaction CS20: בחצי העליון מגדירים קריטריוני בחירה, בתחתון את השינויים (בחרו לחצן רדיו מתאים).

**הערת יועץ:** ה-BOM הוא לב-מבנה-המוצר, ושלושת-הפרמטרים — BOM Usage (1=ייצור), Valid From, ו-Alternative BOM — הם המפתח. מנקודת-מבט-מעשית, ה-usage קובע היכן-ה-BOM-זמין (ייצור, SD, costing, PM), וה-BOM-ים-החלופיים (עד-99) מאפשרים ייצור-אותו-מוצר במספר-דרכים. יועץ מנוסה מנצל תוקף-תאריכי (date-effectivity) לניהול-שינויי-הנדסה, ומתאם עם CO את-ה-costing-BOM, שכן ה-BOM הוא הבסיס לחישוב-עלות-החומר. פסולת-ברמת-הרכיב (component scrap) כאן משפיעה ישירות על-כמויות-ה-MRP.

sections.title: Work Center
sections.en: 6.2.3 Work Center A work center can be a production facility, a processing unit, a machine or group of machines, or even a laborer or group of laborers directly involved in the production process. It’s also possible to group together machines and laborers in a single work cen- ter. To create a work center, follow menu path Logistics  Production  Master Data  Work Centers  Work Center  Create or use Transaction CR01. Note For process industries, create a resource by following menu path Logistics  Production – Process  Master Data  Resources  Resource  Resource  Create or using Transaction CRC1. © 207 6.2 Master Data On the initial screen, enter Plant “1710” for the relevant new work center. It’s manda- tory to assign a plant while creating a work center. Enter the Work Center as “ASSEM- BLY.” This is an alphanumeric identification to denote a work center. Enter “0001” in the Work Center Category field; this is a control function used to ensure that only the relevant screens are eventually available during work center creation. Work center cat- egory 0001 denotes a machine, whereas 0007 denotes a production line. Other important functions on the screen are Copy from Plant and Copy from Work Cen- ter. Check the boxes of the reference work center views that need to be copied to the new work center. These functions help in reducing data entry efforts during the new work center creation by automatically making available all of the necessary informa- tion from the reference work center to the new work center, which you can change as needed. In the following sections, we’ll cover the various tabs that are available in a work center and the data to be maintained, as well as the data’s impact on business processes. Basic Data Choose the Basic Data tab of the work center and enter a short description of the work center. In the Usage field, enter “009” (see Figure 6.10). A usage is a control function that controls whether this work center eventually becomes available for various other tasks, such as the creation of a routing or the production version. Entering usage 009 denotes using this work center in all task list types. Two important fields on this screen are as follows (but not shown):  Shift Note Type A shift note is an option to record the important shift-related details of a work center. These can be general details of the shift, as well as any specific problems encoun- tered at this specific work center during the production process.  Shift Report Type A shift report compiles and consolidates all of the information from a single shift note or multiple shift notes. It is available either in PDF format or other formats, as well as in the layout defined for a company. The user can also digitally sign a shift report before a printout is possible and send a shift report by email. Recall from Chapter 3 that we discussed the configuration of the Standard Value Key field, in which you entered “SAP1.” The standard value key consists of three activities to note and record during the production process when the ASSEMBLY work center was used. A standard value key denotes activities performed at the work center, as well as the option to record them or not. Some of the activities are production time, setup time, processing time, and labor time. If you enter “SAP1,” the system automatically brings up three activities (Setup, Machine, and Labor) for which the actual details in the confirmation process are recorded (see Figure 6.10). 6 Production Planning for Discrete Manufacturing 208 Figure 6.10 Basic Data View of Work Center You should enter “Machine” under Key Word and select 3 must be entered under Rule for Maint. If you mark this activity as must be entered, then during the creation of a routing, the production supervisor will be required to enter the actual duration of the activity; otherwise, the system won’t allow you to save the routing. Other maintenance options are may not be entered, should not be entered, and should be entered, which offer various degrees of control, from an information message to a warning message, if the requisite information (duration, in this case) isn’t recorded during confirmation. In addition, you should check the Backflush box on this screen so that the system will automatically issue components at the work center (in this example, ASSEMBLY) during the confirmation process. © 209 6.2 Master Data Note In Chapter 3, we made the field settings that require the selection of the Backflush field. Default Values Choose the Default Values tab to see the options shown in Figure 6.11. Figure 6.11 Default Values View of Work Center Assign the Control key “PP01” to the work center. A control key is a control function that determines whether a production supervisor can perform an activity or a task associ- ated with the work center or not. A control key controls several functions, such as scheduling, cost, automatic GR, print confirmation, and print. If you don’t check any of the boxes of the control key, then those steps or functions can’t be performed at this work center (ASSEMBLY). For example, if the Scheduling box isn’t checked in the con- trol key, then the system won’t perform scheduling at this work center. Note Chapter 3, Section 3.3.6, covers how to configure a control key. Capacities Choose the Capacities tab to see the options shown in Figure 6.12. Enter “SAP005” in Setup Formula, which denotes the setup formula that the system will use during capacity calculation. For the Processing Formula, enter “SAP006,” and for the Teardown Formula, enter “SAP007.” These formula entries are for Capacity category 001, which is Machine. 6 Production Planning for Discrete Manufacturing 210 Figure 6.12 Capacities View of Work Center Note See Chapter 16 for details about capacity requirements planning. Choose Capacity Header on the toolbar at the bottom of the Capacities tab to open the Change Work Center Capacity: Header screen for Work Center ASSEMBLY (see Figure 6.13). Figure 6.13 Capacity Header © 211 6.2 Master Data The capacity header contains comprehensive capacity details, such as the start and end time of shifts and breaks, the overload percentage allowed for capacity, shifts and inter- vals, and the factory calendar. Note Refer to Chapter 2 for information about setting up the factory calendar and capacity planner group. For this example, you should maintain the following in each field:  Short Text for Capacity: “Assembly” This short text describes the capacity category—for example, a specific production line or machine.  Capacity Responsible: “A” It’s important to assign a capacity planner group to a work center so that during evaluation of capacities, the capacity planner group can be one of the evaluation cri- teria. The capacity planner group shouldn’t be the name of the person but instead the name of the area or domain of responsibilities.  Grouping If, apart from the normal shift timings during the entire calendar year (per the fac- tory calendar), a company has any specific slow or busy seasons in which either an increase or a decrease in the number of shifts or intervals takes place, then a produc- tion planner can logically group these by using the grouping function. For example, in several countries, workers have longer breaks on Fridays, and in other countries, Saturday is a half working day. You can address such business scenarios by using grouping, which doesn’t fall under normal start, finish, and break timings.  Factory Calendar ID: “US” This is the same factory calendar configured in Chapter 2; now, you’re assigning it to the work center.  Capacity Base Unit: “MIN” (for minutes) This is the unit of measure (in hours) in which the system displays the capacity of a work center.  Start Time: “07:00:00” This is the start time of a shift of a work center.  End Time: “16:00:00” This is the end time of a shift of a work center.  Length of breaks: “01:00:00” This is the total length of all breaks during the start and end of shifts. Break timing deducts the availability time of the capacity of a production line. For example, if a machine runs 12 hours a day, with two hours of daily breaks, then the available capacity of the production line is 10 hours. 6 Production Planning for Discrete Manufacturing 212  Capacity Utilization: “100” (percent) This is the actual capacity utilization factor. This factor has to be as realistic and as close to the actual capacity of a production line as possible to enable the system to calculate the available capacity of the production line. We recommend that you model for statistically unforeseen downtimes. When the SAP S/4HANA system has built up a significant amount of data, use one of many available statistics reports on capacities to update the information in this field. For example, say that a capacity planner has maintained a value of 100% in this field but the statistical reports reveal that the actually utilized capacity is never more than 90%. In this case, updating the information to 90% here ensures realistic and practical capacity planning, and there will be greater confidence in the system-generated results. (Refer to Chapter 19 on reporting.)  No. Ind. Capacities: “1” This is the number of individual capacities associated with a production line. For example, if four individual ice cream mixers are created as one production line, then the individual capacities are four in number and directly multiplied by the timings of the capacity of the production line. As another example, if the available capacity of a production line is 10 hours in a day, and if there are four individual capacities, then the total available capacity of the production line is 40 hours. If you will be using splitting in a routing and you will also define the number of splits, then it’s important to also define the number of capacities because the system checks for this information during scheduling.  Relevant to Finite Scheduling (not shown) Checking this box causes the work center to consider capacity overload during capacity evaluation.  Overload: “5%” (not shown) Setting a capacity overload in percentage terms directly increases the capacity avail- ability of the production line by the defined percentage. If, for example, the total capacity of a production line is 40 hours with 10% overload, then the available capac- ity is 44 hours. A 10% overload of 40 hours is four hours, and it adds up to 40 hours to show the total available capacity at 44 hours.  Long-Term Planning (not shown) Checking this box enables the system to consider the production line availability during long-term planning. Long-term planning typically is a simulative planning of material and production lines over a longer period. Next, click the Intervals button, and then, on the screen shown in Figure 6.14, you can assign specific intervals or shifts that are applicable to the defined duration. For this example, you should define that from 01/01/2025 until 04/02/2025, there will be a shift Sequence consisting of a seven-day cycle (Length of cycle). © 213 6.2 Master Data Figure 6.14 Interval in Capacity Header Scheduling Next, click the Back icon, and then, choose the Scheduling tab to see the options shown in Figure 6.15. Enter the standard formulas available for discrete manufacturing, which we covered in detail in Chapter 3. Figure 6.15 Scheduling View of Work Center Costing Choose the Costing tab to see the options shown in Figure 6.16. Because PP compre- hensively integrates with product cost controlling’s cost object controlling (part of SAP S/4HANA Finance), each work center needs to have a cost center. One cost center can be assigned to multiple work centers, but multiple cost centers cannot be assigned to a work center. 6 Production Planning for Discrete Manufacturing 214 Figure 6.16 Costing View of Work Center Note You should coordinate with a CO expert to ensure that each cost center and associated activity type for the given controlling area has price planning. In the same step, you should ensure that activity types and cost centers are already in place so that you can assign them in the work center. This is an integration point between PP and CO. Enter the following details:  Start date: “01/01/2024” This is the start date of the availability of the cost center for the work center.  End Date: “12/31/9999” This is the end date of the availability of the cost center for the production line.  Cost Center: “17101301” Every work center needs to have a cost center directly assigned to it so that when work is performed using the work center, the system is able to accumulate all of the costs in the designated cost center.  Activity Type (Alt: Activity Text Setup): “3” The activity type denotes the predefined rate at which the system calculates the costs incurred to perform machine setup. Repeat the same process of entering activity types and formulas for the other remain- ing two activities, Machine and Labor, and then save the work center. © 215 6.2 Master Data

מרכז עבודה (Work Center) יכול להיות מתקן ייצור, יחידת עיבוד, מכונה/קבוצת מכונות, או עובד/קבוצת עובדים המעורבים ישירות בייצור; ניתן גם לקבץ מכונות ועובדים יחד. ליצירה: Logistics • Production • Master Data • Work Centers • Work Center • Create, או Transaction CR01.
**הערה:** לתעשיות תהליך, צרו משאב (resource): Logistics • Production – Process • Master Data • Resources • Resource • Create, או Transaction CRC1.
במסך ההתחלתי הזינו Plant "1710" (חובה). הזינו Work Center "ASSEMBLY" (זיהוי אלפאנומרי). הזינו "0001" ב-Work Center Category — בקרה שמבטיחה זמינות מסכים רלוונטיים; 0001 = מכונה, ‏0007 = קו ייצור. פונקציות Copy from Plant ו-Copy from Work Center מפחיתות עבודת הזנה.

**Basic Data:** הזינו תיאור קצר. בשדה Usage הזינו "009" (Figure 6.10) — בקרה לזמינות בכל סוגי רשימות המשימות. שדות חשובים: Shift Note Type (רישום פרטי משמרת); Shift Report Type (איחוד הערות משמרת ל-PDF, חתימה דיגיטלית, שליחה במייל). שדה Standard Value Key — הזנת "SAP1" (מפרק 3) מביא אוטומטית שלוש פעילויות (Setup, ‏Machine, ‏Labor) לרישום באישור. הזינו "Machine" תחת Key Word ובחרו 3 must be entered ב-Rule for Maint. — אז ביצירת מסלול, חובה להזין את משך הפעילות. אפשרויות אחרות: may not be entered, ‏should not be entered, ‏should be entered. סמנו את תיבת Backflush — המערכת תנפיק רכיבים אוטומטית ב-ASSEMBLY באישור (הגדרת השדה בפרק 3).

**Default Values (Figure 6.11):** הקצו Control key "PP01" — בקרה אם מפקח יכול לבצע פעילות/משימה. שולט בתזמון, עלות, GR אוטומטי, אישור הדפסה והדפסה. אם תיבה לא מסומנת, השלב לא יבוצע (למשל ללא Scheduling — אין תזמון). (תצורת מפתח בקרה — פרק 3.3.6.)

**Capacities (Figure 6.12):** הזינו Setup Formula "SAP005", ‏Processing Formula "SAP006", ‏Teardown Formula "SAP007" — לחישוב קיבולת, ל-Capacity category 001 (Machine). (פרק 16 — תכנון דרישות קיבולת.) בחרו Capacity Header (Figure 6.13):
• Short Text for Capacity: "Assembly".
• Capacity Responsible: "A" (קבוצת מתכנן קיבולת — שם תחום ולא אדם).
• Grouping: לקיבוץ עונות איטיות/עמוסות החורגות ממשמרות רגילות.
• Factory Calendar ID: "US" (מפרק 2).
• Capacity Base Unit: "MIN".
• Start Time "07:00:00", ‏End Time "16:00:00", ‏Length of breaks "01:00:00" (מנכה מזמינות הקיבולת — מכונה 12 שעות עם שעתיים הפסקות = 10 שעות זמינות).
• Capacity Utilization: "100" (אחוז — ככל שמדויק לקיבולת בפועל, התכנון אמין יותר; עדכנו לפי דוחות סטטיסטיים).
• No. Ind. Capacities: "1" (מספר הקיבולות הבודדות בקו; 10 שעות × 4 קיבולות = 40 שעות; חשוב להגדיר אם משתמשים בפיצול).
• Relevant to Finite Scheduling: סימון = שקילת עומס-יתר בהערכה.
• Overload: "5%" (מגדיל ישירות את זמינות הקיבולת; 40 שעות + 10% = 44).
• Long-Term Planning: שקילת זמינות הקו בתכנון ארוך-טווח.
בלחצן Intervals (Figure 6.14) מקצים משמרות/אינטרוולים לטווח (בדוגמה, מ-01/01/2025 עד 04/02/2025, רצף בן מחזור שבעה ימים).

**Scheduling (Figure 6.15):** הזינו את הנוסחאות הסטנדרטיות לייצור בדיד (פרק 3).

**Costing (Figure 6.16):** מאחר ש-PP משולב עם בקרת עלות מוצר, כל מרכז עבודה צריך מרכז עלות. מרכז עלות אחד ניתן להקצאה למספר מרכזי עבודה, אך לא להפך. (תאמו עם מומחה CO לתכנון מחירי מרכז עלות וסוגי פעילות — נקודת אינטגרציה PP/CO.) הזינו: Start date "01/01/2024"; End Date "12/31/9999"; Cost Center "17101301"; Activity Type "3" (התעריף לחישוב עלות ה-setup). חזרו על התהליך לפעילויות Machine ו-Labor ושמרו.

**הערת יועץ:** מרכז-העבודה מגשר בין PP ל-CO — הוא נושא את-מפתחות-הבקרה (control keys), את-ה-SVK (ערכי-תקן), ואת-הקישור למרכז-העלות-ולתעריפי-הפעילות. מנקודת-מבט-אינטגרטיבית, כל-שעת-מכונה-או-עבודה שמאשרים מתומחרת לפי-התעריף המקושר-כאן, ולכן שגיאה בקישור מרכז-עבודה↔מרכז-עלות משבשת את-חישוב-העלות-בפועל. יועץ מנוסה מתאם את-הקטגוריה (0001=מכונה, 0007=קו) ואת-ה-usage (009=כל-רשימות-המשימות) עם-מבנה-הייצור-הפיזי, ומוודא שתעריפי-הפעילות תוחזקו ב-CO לפני-תחילת-האישורים — אחרת האישורים ייכשלו ב-COFC.

sections.title: Routing
sections.en: 6.2.4 Routing The routing of a material can contain a series of operations. The operation details are defined for each operation based on the production quantity, production time, and associated unit of measure. You assign work centers to the routing, which should also contain an SVK, in which the standard values for setup time, production time, and tear- down time are defined. The routing is the sequence of logical production processes through which a product will, for example, be transformed from a raw material into a finished product. To create the routing of a material, follow menu path Logistics  Production  Master Data  Routings  Routings  Standard Routings  Create or use Transaction CA01. Figure 6.17 shows the initial screen you use to create a routing. Enter the Material as “FG129” and the Plant as “1710.” In the Key Date field, enter “06/27/2024” to denote the date when the routing becomes available in the production process. Because the rout- ing validity starts on June 27, 2024 (06/27/2024), if a production planner creates a pro- duction order for the month of January 2024, this routing won’t be available. Figure 6.17 Initial Screen for Routing If you don’t enter a date during routing creation, then the system automatically assigns the routing’s creation date as the valid from date. The following sections will discuss the various elements and options that are available in the routing. Header Details Next, choose Routings. In the header details of the routing, shown in Figure 6.18, enter the following: 6 Production Planning for Discrete Manufacturing 216  Usage: “1” (for Production) This makes the routing available during subsequent production activities, in which the system uses the routing during production order creation.  Overall Status: “4” (for Released) This makes the routing available during subsequent production activities, in which the system uses the routing during creation of the production order. If the overall status of the routing is set to Being Created (1), it won’t be available when you create a production order for the material.  Planning Work Center: “ASSEMBLY” This is the work center that was previously created and is now used in the planning and production of the material. Figure 6.18 Header Details in Routing Note Normally, a production planner should have several work centers already created before creating a routing. You should either leave the Planning Work Center field open or blank or make it include the “bottleneck” work center that the production planner wants to evaluate during the planning process. © 217 6.2 Master Data The Lot Size From field denotes that the smallest quantity of the production order must be at least 1 PC for the system to consider using this routing. The Lot Size To field denotes the maximum quantity of the production/order. The Parameters for Dynamic Modification/Inspection Points area of the screen (not shown but located further down the same screen) is the integration point between PP and QM in SAP S/4HANA. The parameters entered there determine whether the system carries out an inspection for the inspection type, for the individual inspection lot, or for the master inspection characteristics. Note Because QM also integrates with discrete manufacturing, we recommend that you engage a QM expert for this activity. Next, click the Operation button to access the screen in Figure 6.19, where you can maintain the Work Center as “ASSEMBLY.” This denotes assigning a previously created work center to an operation, which is used in the production of material and for which the routing is being created. An operation defines, for example, a single-level detail of a production step. The second work center, Work, denotes the second step in the produc- tion process. Then, you should double-click Operation 0010, which opens the screen in Figure 6.20. Figure 6.19 Operations Overview of Routing Operations Figure 6.20 shows the detailed operations view for maintaining the following entries:  Setup: “50 MIN” Here, you define the time it takes to set up the machine for this task. Any deviation in setup time, either positive or negative, has a direct impact on the costs of goods manufactured (COGM).  Act. Type: “3” An activity type is a result of the direct integration of PP with the product cost con- trolling functionality. In fact, PP completely integrates with product cost con- trolling. An activity type contains the financial rate (value based) to perform an 6 Production Planning for Discrete Manufacturing 218 activity during production. So, five hours of production time has an associated cost of producing the material. Any deviation in production time, either positive or neg- ative, has a direct implication for the COGM.  Machine: “150 MIN” Recall that you defined in the work center (in the rule for maintenance, when you selected the Must Be Entered option) that recording duration information in the routing is mandatory, so it’s mandatory to define the time the operation will take in this work center’s manufacturing process.  Labor: “150 MIN” Here, you define the time it takes to dismantle or tear down the setup of the machine or the production line. Any deviation in teardown time, either positive or negative, has a direct implication on COGM. Figure 6.20 Operation Details in Routing Enter the Act. Type for each of the three activities: Setup, Machine, and Labor. These durations are for the Base Quantity of 10 PC of material FG129 produced. Notice that the system automatically incorporates the Control Key that was defined in the work center, ASSEMBLY, in the previous step. © 219 6.2 Master Data Next, scroll down to see the screen area shown in Figure 6.21. There, you assign the reduction strategy that was configured for plant 1710 in Chapter 3. If you check the Tear- down/Wait Parallel (simulation) box here, it enables a planner to see simulated details during scheduling. You can also define normal and minimum interoperation times. The interoperation times consist of wait time, queue time, and move (transport) time. During reduction—that is, during scheduling conflicts in basic dates—the system switches to minimum interoperation times and performs further reduction based on the reduction strategy and the defined reduction levels. Next, scroll down the same screen to see the screen areas shown in Figure 6.22. With Splitting, a production planner can divide a large production lot into several smaller lots, provided that there are several individual capacities to manage it. The system checks the number of splits with individual capacities defined in the work center. With Overlapping, the system passes the processed parts of the total lot directly on to the next machine. You should define the minimum overlap time and the minimum send-ahead quantity to the next operation if there’s a business need for it. Figure 6.21 Operation Details in Routing: Interoperation Times 6 Production Planning for Discrete Manufacturing 220 Figure 6.22 Item Details in Routing: Splitting and Overlapping The information in the General data tab (see Figure 6.23) relates to the percentage scrap (planned) for the operation and integrating with the human resources (HR) system. For example, the person doing confirmation on the shop floor can be integrated with the HR system. Figure 6.23 Item Details in Routing: General Data © 221 6.2 Master Data Next, scroll down further on the same screen to see the screen area shown in Figure 6.24. Here, you can check the Subcontracting box to reflect the details that can be main- tained in case the material processing involves subcontracting. A subcontracting pro- cess entails engaging the services of a service provider to perform some of the steps in the production process, which happens when either there isn’t an in-house expert available or the company finds it more cost effective to outsource those steps. Figure 6.24 Item Details in Routing: Subcontracting Check the Subcontracting box and maintain the procurement details in the remaining fields. When a production planner creates a production order for the material, the sys- tem will simultaneously create a purchase requisition for the subcontracting opera- tions. You can use the User-Specific Fields section (not shown) to maintain additional details related to routing that can’t be maintained elsewhere. Components Assignment Next, press (F6) or follow menu path Goto  Operations Overview, and the system will bring you back to the Operations Overview screen. On this screen, choose Components Allocation to open the screen shown in Figure 6.25. Here, you can find the component allocation in routing. These components are directly taken from a material’s BOM, 6 Production Planning for Discrete Manufacturing 222 which you created in the previous step. If you don’t assign a specific component to a specific operation, then the system assigns all components to the first operation of the routing during lead-time scheduling. This means that all components must be avail- able at the first operation so that during backflush, the system can consume all compo- nents in the first operation during its confirmation. Figure 6.25 Material Component Overview If your company’s business process entails that a few components are used or needed in the later stages of the production process, then you should select them and use the Reassign button to assign specific components to the operation. For this example, assign Component 50 to Oper./Act. 0020. This means that while the system will con- sume other components in the confirmation of the first operation (0010) using the backflush functionality, it will consume component 50 when the user confirms opera- tion 0020. To ensure that the system uses the backflush functionality, check the Back- flushing box. If a component’s quantity is maintained with a negative value—say, 50,000 KG—it denotes a by-product being produced in the production process. So, although all components in a material BOM are consumed during the production pro- cess, the coproducts or by-products are generated or produced. Material Assignment If you go back to the routing header screen and choose MatlAssignment, the popup shown in Figure 6.26 will appear. Material FG129 in Plnt 1710 is assigned an internal group of 41710010 with the group counter (GrC) set to 1. Later, we’ll use this group (41710010) and the group counter (1) to create the next PP master data element, which is the production version. It’s important to add that every combination of a group and a group counter reflects certain planned working processes. You can assign several materials together with their respective plants to this routing group. All such materials belonging to this routing group will have the same group but will have ascending group counter numbers. © 223 6.2 Master Data Figure 6.26 Material Assignment Tips and Tricks If there are several materials undergoing the same production process, there’s no longer a need to create separate routings for each. Just create one routing and assign relevant materials (with plants) to it. This saves you time and effort in creating an important mas- ter data element (routing) and also eliminates or reduces redundant data entry efforts. Sequences Whenever we refer to routing, we imply that it will be a sequence of operations in a log- ical order. For example, when we define operations 10, 20, and 30 for a routing, we indi- cate that operation 10 will be the first step of the production process, operation 20 will be the second step, and operation 30 will be the third step. This also means that we con- firm the operations in the same sequence. However, you can also maintain parallel and alternative sequences in routing. Parallel sequences enable you to split up the produc- tion process if you can carry out specific production steps of an order simultaneously. Alternative sequences represent alternatives that enable you to produce a product in the production process in different ways. You can call the sequence overview by choosing the Sequences icon on the initial rout- ing screen. The sequence overview will display all parallel and alternative sequences contained in the routing:  The system numbers the sequences and also contains a sequence category. The stan- dard sequence contains sequence category 0.  The parallel sequences contain sequence category 1.  The alternative sequences contain sequence category 2. When you first create a routing and define an operation, the system contains a stan- dard sequence. When you click the New Entries button, a popup will appear for you to select either Alternative Sequence or Parallel Sequence. For this example, choose Alter- native Sequence (see Figure 6.27) and the system will navigate to the screen shown in Figure 6.28. 6 Production Planning for Discrete Manufacturing 224 Figure 6.27 Choosing Sequence Category In Figure 6.28, Sequence 1 refers to the first sequence after the original operation’s sequence, which is 0. The Branch Operation field stipulates the operation during which the system should proceed with the parallel sequence. The Return Operation field denotes the operation number that the system must return to or branch back to after the parallel operation. It’s mandatory to define the return operation. Figure 6.28 Sequence Details Figure 6.28 shows a sequence overview for material FG129. It stipulates that the system will branch off to an alternative sequence on operation 0010 and will return to a stan- dard sequence in operation 0020. For the alternative sequence, you can define the min- imum and maximum lot sizes (Lot Size From and Lot Size To) that are applicable to the alternative sequence. © 225 6.2 Master Data Production Resources and Tools Production resources and tools (PRTs) are movable operating resources that you can assign to internal and external operations in the routing. Examples of PRTs include tools, materials, documents or drawings, and test equipment. PRTs play an important role in facilitating the production process. For example, to move heavy metal contain- ers from one production line to the next, you need a pair of large metal hooks, which are PRTs. You can assign a PRT to an operation of a routing by choosing the PRT icon. On the screen shown in Figure 6.29, assign a Material PRT of “RM29” and assign a Quantity of “1.000.” You can use this screen to create more PRTs, such as documents and equip- ment, by clicking the corresponding Document and Equipment buttons. Figure 6.29 PRT Assignment Delete Task List One of the advantages of PP master data is that you can delete the master data from the system, which means you don’t have to archive it. You can also delete problematic master data—for example, a wrongly created a work center or an incorrect routing— plus any PP master data that isn’t in use. To delete a routing or, in fact, any task lists (e.g., rate routing, master recipe, inspection plan), use Transaction CA98. On the initial screen, enter the selection parameters and choose the relevant deletion options. 6 Production Planning for Discrete Manufacturing 226 Engineering Workbench You can use the Engineering Workbench to create or make changes to PP master data, such as BOMs or routings. The Engineering Workbench is an interactive and intuitive tool that lets you make collective changes to, for example, BOM headers of several materials at once. Use Transaction CEWB to access the Engineering Workbench. Then, in the initial popup, select the work area to work on. The work area can be the BOM header, BOM item, rout- ing header, or routing item. On the parameter selection screen, enter the parameters and then choose Load BOMs and Task Lists. In the ensuing worklist, make the desired changes to PP master data or create a new worklist.

מסלול הייצור (Routing) של חומר מכיל סדרת פעולות. פרטי כל פעולה מוגדרים לפי כמות ייצור, זמן ייצור ויחידת מידה. מקצים מרכזי עבודה למסלול, שצריך גם לכלול SVK עם ערכי תקן ל-setup/production/teardown. המסלול הוא רצף תהליכי הייצור הלוגיים.
ליצירה: Logistics • Production • Master Data • Routings • Routings • Standard Routings • Create, או Transaction CA01. ב-Figure 6.17 הזינו Material "FG129", ‏Plant "1710", ובשדה Key Date "06/27/2024" (התאריך שממנו המסלול זמין). אם לא ניתן תאריך, המערכת מקצה את תאריך היצירה.

**Header Details (Figure 6.18):** Usage "1" (Production — זמין ביצירת הזמנה); Overall Status "4" (Released; אם 1 = Being Created, לא יהיה זמין); Planning Work Center "ASSEMBLY". (השאירו את השדה ריק או הזינו את מרכז ה"צוואר בקבוק".) שדה Lot Size From = הכמות המינימלית להזמנה (לפחות 1 PC); Lot Size To = המקסימלית. אזור Parameters for Dynamic Modification/Inspection Points הוא נקודת אינטגרציה PP/QM (תאמו עם מומחה QM).
לחצו Operation (Figure 6.19) — תחזקו Work Center "ASSEMBLY". פעולה מגדירה שלב ייצור חד-רמתי. לחצו פעמיים על Operation 0010 (Figure 6.20).

**Operations (Figure 6.20):** Setup "50 MIN" (זמן הקמת המכונה; כל סטייה משפיעה ישירות על COGM); Act. Type "3" (תוצאת אינטגרציית PP עם בקרת עלות — מכיל את התעריף הכספי לביצוע פעילות); Machine "150 MIN" (חובה כי הוגדר Must Be Entered במרכז העבודה); Labor "150 MIN". הזינו Act. Type לכל אחת מהשלוש. המשכים אלו ל-Base Quantity של 10 PC של FG129. המערכת משלבת אוטומטית את ה-Control Key שהוגדר ב-ASSEMBLY.
גללו (Figure 6.21) — הקצו את אסטרטגיית ההפחתה (מפרק 3). סימון Teardown/Wait Parallel מאפשר תצוגת סימולציה בתזמון. הגדירו זמני בין-פעולה (interoperation) רגילים ומינימליים — wait, ‏queue, ‏move (transport). בהפחתה (בקונפליקט תאריכים בסיסיים), המערכת עוברת לזמני מינימום.
גללו (Figure 6.22): ב-Splitting, המתכנן מחלק אצווה גדולה לקטנות אם יש קיבולות בודדות (המערכת בודקת מול מספר הקיבולות במרכז העבודה). ב-Overlapping, המערכת מעבירה חלקים מעובדים ישירות למכונה הבאה (הגדירו זמן חפיפה מינימלי וכמות send-ahead מינימלית).
בלשונית General data (Figure 6.23) — אחוז פסולת מתוכננת לפעולה ואינטגרציה עם HR. גללו (Figure 6.24) — סמנו Subcontracting לפרטי קבלנות משנה (העסקת ספק שירות לחלק משלבי הייצור). בסימון ותחזוקת פרטי הרכש, ביצירת הזמנה המערכת תיצור במקביל דרישת רכש לפעולות קבלנות המשנה.

**Components Assignment:** F6 או Goto • Operations Overview, ואז Components Allocation (Figure 6.25). הרכיבים נלקחים ישירות מ-BOM החומר. אם לא מקצים רכיב לפעולה ספציפית, המערכת מקצה את כולם לפעולה הראשונה בתזמון lead-time. בדוגמה, הקצו Component 50 ל-Oper./Act. 0020 (כפתור Reassign) — המערכת תצרוך אותו באישור פעולה 0020. סמנו Backflushing. אם כמות רכיב שלילית (למשל –50,000 KG), זה מציין תוצר לוואי המיוצר.

**Material Assignment:** בכותרת המסלול, MatlAssignment (Figure 6.26). FG129 ב-Plnt 1710 מוקצה לקבוצה פנימית 41710010 עם group counter (GrC) ‏1. נשתמש ב-group (41710010) וב-counter (1) ליצירת גרסת הייצור. ניתן להקצות מספר חומרים (עם מפעליהם) לאותה קבוצת מסלול — כולם עם אותה קבוצה אך counter עולה.
**Tips and Tricks:** אם מספר חומרים עוברים אותו תהליך, צרו מסלול אחד והקצו אליו את החומרים — חוסך זמן ומפחית כפילות.

**Sequences:** מסלול הוא רצף פעולות לוגי (10, 20, 30). ניתן לתחזק רצפים מקבילים וחלופיים. רצפים מקבילים מפצלים את התהליך אם ניתן לבצע שלבים בו-זמנית; חלופיים מייצגים דרכי ייצור שונות. קוראים לסקירת הרצפים בסמל Sequences. סוגי רצף: סטנדרטי = 0; מקביל = 1; חלופי = 2. ב-New Entries בוחרים Alternative או Parallel Sequence (Figure 6.27 → 6.28). ב-Figure 6.28, Sequence 1 הוא הרצף הראשון אחרי המקורי (0). שדה Branch Operation = הפעולה שבה המערכת ממשיכה לרצף המקביל; Return Operation = הפעולה לחזרה (חובה). בדוגמה, המערכת מסתעפת לרצף חלופי בפעולה 0010 וחוזרת לסטנדרטי בפעולה 0020. ניתן להגדיר Lot Size From/To לרצף החלופי.

**Production Resources and Tools (PRTs):** משאבי תפעול ניידים הניתנים להקצאה לפעולות פנימיות וחיצוניות (כלים, חומרים, מסמכים/שרטוטים, ציוד בדיקה). בסמל PRT (Figure 6.29), הקצו Material PRT "RM29" וכמות "1.000". ניתן ליצור עוד PRTs (Document ו-Equipment).

**Delete Task List:** ניתן למחוק נתוני אב PP (אין צורך בארכוב) — מרכז עבודה/מסלול שגויים או שאינם בשימוש. למחיקת מסלול או כל task list (rate routing, master recipe, inspection plan): Transaction CA98.

**Engineering Workbench:** ליצירה/שינוי נתוני אב PP (BOMים, מסלולים) — כלי אינטראקטיבי לשינויים קולקטיביים (למשל כותרות BOM של מספר חומרים). Transaction CEWB — בחרו את אזור העבודה (BOM header/item, ‏routing header/item), הזינו פרמטרים, Load BOMs and Task Lists, ובצעו שינויים.

**הערת יועץ:** המסלול הוא רצף-הפעולות שמזין את-התזמון-ואת-הקיבולת, וה-Overall Status הוא מלכודת-נפוצה: אם הוא 1 (Being Created) ולא-4 (Released), המסלול לא-יהיה-זמין ביצירת-ההזמנה. מנקודת-מבט-מעשית, ה-usage (1=ייצור), ה-lot-size-range, ומרכז-העבודה-המתכנן הם המפתח. יועץ מנוסה מקפיד על-סטטוס-4, מגדיר את-מרכז-ה'צוואר-בקבוק' כמרכז-מתכנן, ומתאם את-אזור ה-inspection-points עם-QM. המסלול הוא גם-הבסיס-ל-SVK, ולכן דיוק-ערכי-התקן בו קובע את-דיוק-התזמון-ואת-חישוב-עלות-הפעילות.

sections.title: Production Versions
sections.en: 6.2.5 Production Versions Production versions denote different ways in which a company produces a material. This includes, for example, a material with one routing but multiple BOMs. Hence, for each BOM and the same routing, the system needs a separate production version to denote the uniqueness of the different ways to produce the same material. The requirement to create a separate production version also applies when there is one BOM for a material but multiple routings. In SAP S/4HANA, it’s now mandatory to create and make avail- able a production version for all three manufacturing types (discrete, process, and repet- itive). The salient features of the production version include the following:  Production versions can be quantity range specific and thus act as control functions. For example, you can create one production version that has a quantity limitation of 1 to 1,000 PC and another production version for quantities greater than 1,000 PC.  Production versions can also be validity period specific and thus act as control func- tions. For example, there may be one production version that is valid from April 1, 2024, until March 31, 2025. From April 1, 2025, onward, there may be a new produc- tion version. When the system has to assign a production version to the production order, it searches for specific validity dates. When the system finds the relevant pro- duction version, it automatically assigns it.  If the system can find multiple production versions fulfilling the search and applica- tion criteria, it assigns the first available production version to the production order. To facilitate production version creation in SAP S/4HANA, a new report, report CS_ BOM_PRODVER_MIGRATION, is available. To execute the report/worklist, you use Transaction SE38, enter “CS_BOM_PRODVER_MIGRATION” on the screen that appears, and choose Execute or press (F8). On the next screen that appears, choose materials and the associated plants; alternatively, you can simply enter a plant to bring up all the materials for which BOMs exist and the qualities for production version creation. To simulate production version creation, choose the Run in Simulation Mode radio button © 227 6.2 Master Data and then choose Execute. To create production versions in actual mode, choose the Run in Actual Mode radio button. A production planner can choose to approve the creation of individual, selective, or all production versions and then choose Approve. A message will then appear to confirm creation of the production version. To create a new production version, follow menu path Logistics  Production  Master Data  Production Versions or use Transaction C223. In the Selection Conditions area of Figure 6.30, enter the Plant as “1710,”, enter the Material as “FG129,” and then press (Enter). If the system can’t find any production ver- sion for the material, then the lower half of the screen will be blank. If it does find ver- sions, then the system will display the relevant production versions. Figure 6.30 Production Version Initial Screen On the menu bar in the center of the production version creation screen, you have just about all of the options you’ll normally need when creating production version master data. This includes copying, deleting, copying from a template, and so on. Choose Cre- ate Production Version to open the screen shown in Figure 6.31. Enter the basic details, such as Plant “1710,” Production Version “0001,” Production Version Text, Valid from “10/05/2017,” and Valid to “12/31/9999.” Figure 6.31 Overview Screen of Production Version Next, you should either select the first line item and double-click it or choose the Detail icon. This will bring up the screen in Figure 6.32. 6 Production Planning for Discrete Manufacturing 228 Figure 6.32 Detailed Screen of Production Version Next, enter the details listed in Table 6.2. Field Value Additional Details/Remarks Material FG129 – Production Version 0001 – Valid From 10/05/2023 This field contains the starting validity date of the pro- duction version. Valid To 12/31/9999 This field contains the ending validity date of the pro- duction version. Detailed Planning Routing (N) Task list type N represents a routing. Each task list type represents a different function. Type list type R represents a rate routing, whereas task list type Q represents a quality inspection task list. Enter the routing that you created in the previous step. For this example, enter routing Group “41710010” and a Group Counter of “1.” Alternative BOM 1 This is the BOM that you created in the previous step. BOM Usage 1 This field contains the BOM usage, where 1 refers to the usage production. Table 6.2 Entering Parameters in Production Version © 229 6.2 Master Data The Lock field provides the flexibility to lock or unlock the production version anytime to allow or restrict access to the production version during production order creation. A locked production version won’t be available for selection during production order creation. Finally, click the Check button located at the top right-hand side of the screen to evaluate whether the details incorporated in the production version, such as BOM and routing, are correct and valid. It’s important to note here that you can add data in the production version that doesn’t make sense, such as an incorrect work center as a production line. The system then confirms that it’s can find a relevant task list (routing), as well as a BOM, that meets the other criteria of the production version. This includes having validity dates of the routing and the BOM that fall within the validity specified in the production version, as well as the lot sizes mentioned in the production version (see Figure 6.33). Then, choose the Cancel icon. Figure 6.33 Results of Production Version Consistency Check The green traffic lights for the task list and the BOM denote that the consistency check was successful and that this production version will be available to users during pro- duction order creation. If the system returns a warning or error during the consistency 6 Production Planning for Discrete Manufacturing 230 check, it indicates it with a yellow or red traffic light, respectively. In the production version, you can check whether previously created and unchecked production versions are still valid or not. Next, choose Close Detailed Screen and Adopt Changes and save the production version. Note SAP S/4HANA 2023 offers more options to propose production versions based on a com- bination of material groups, plants, and MRP controllers. To make the relevant configu- ration settings, you should use the menu path SAP IMG  Production  Basic Data  Pro- duction Version  Define Rules for Production Version Proposals. The specific values maintained here will take precedence over generic values during production version proposal selection. You can also disable the proposal settings, if and when required. Similarly, you can make relevant configuration settings perform additional checks during the production version consistency check that we just showed you in Figure 6.33. For example, based on the configuration settings you’ve made, the system can issue an error or a warning message whenever it finds an inactive BOM that has been used while creating a production version. You can also make settings that will make the system not check an active or inactive BOM. To make the relevant configuration settings, use menu path SAP IMG  Production  Basic Data  Production Version  Define Inconsistency Checks for Production Versions.
