sections.title: Traffic Lights for Days’ Supply and Receipt Days’ Supply
sections.en: 13.13.2 Traffic Lights for Days’ Supply and Receipt Days’ Supply The red, yellow, and green traffic lights in both Transaction MD06 and Transaction MD07 in Figure 13.65 give a quick indication of potential overstocking or understocking in the list view:  A red light will appear if a demand from the past is still unfulfilled. How far in the past this demand element lies is specified by the negative days of supply shown in a column in the list display.  A green light doesn’t mean everything is in order. It can also mean that there is more stock than needed to fulfill requirements in the future. Green lights, therefore, can alert a planner if there is too much inventory held.  Yellow lights are assigned to materials for which demand and supply are in perfect balance. Figure 13.65 Stock/Requirements List, Collective Access SAP S/4HANA allows you to make changes to the traffic light settings to tell the system when a material’s planning should be alerted with a red or green light and what range is acceptable for an item with balanced demand and supply. You can also develop a traffic light system to provide relevant and useful information. For example, you could consider setting up the list so that traffic lights are sorted with the most urgent material handling on top and long-term opportunities at the bottom. One such scenario could involve setting the monitor so that materials with stock days of supply below safety levels (and not only after they are overdue) would have a red light. Anything that has receipts coming in to cover demand within an acceptable time frame would get a yellow light, and anything that has too many receipts coming too early—and which therefore needs to be expedited out—would get a green light. © 745 13.13 Stock/Requirements List You can also use the traffic lights for exception messages: the exception groups consid- ered more important can be above the ones that aren’t so urgent, combined with the ranges of coverage. In the stock/requirements list or in the MRP list, the system calculates the number of days on the time axis for which the existing stock of material can fulfill the require- ments. Receipt days’ supply indicates how long the current stock and the expected receipts can cover the requirements. The system offers two different types of receipt days’ supply:  Receipt days’ supply 1  Receipt days’ supply 2 You can select the receipt elements for both types of receipt days’ supplies by following menu path SAP IMG  Production  Material Requirements Planning  Evaluation  Define Receipt Elements for Receipt Days’ Supply. In this step, you select which procurement elements the system should consider in or exclude from its calculation for days’ supply. For example, you can define two receipt days’ supplies and instruct the system to take the less binding receipt elements into account for the first receipt day’s supply and take only the binding receipt elements (such as production orders and shipping notifica- tions) into account for the second day’s supply. The Safety Stock field controls whether the days’ stock supply considers safety stock while calculating the number of days until the warehouse stock falls below the safety stock. If the indicator 1 is maintained, then the system uses the number of days until the stock falls below 0.

sections.title: Exception Messages
sections.en: 13.13.3 Exception Messages The system generates exception messages in MRP when it encounters alerts during the planning run. The system displays exception messages for each relevant procurement element in the stock/requirements list (refer to the Exception column in Figure 13.64). You can also view the exception elements by choosing Edit  Find in the List. The main elements of exception messages are priority, assignment to group, suppress message, create MRP list, and text of exception message. Exception messages are dis- played primarily in four transactions:  Transaction MD04 displays the dynamically created stock requirements situations for an individual material  Transaction MD05 displays the MRP list, which is a snapshot from the time when the MRP run last planned the material  Transaction MD06 displays a collective list of materials with their respective MRP lists  Transaction MD07 displays a collective list of materials with their respective stock/ requirements situations 13 Material Requirements Planning 746 Tips and Tricks You can change text of exception messages to denote the importance of an exception. For example, changing the text to “Warning: stock fallen below safety stock level” will help a planner quickly separate exception messages with a warning from exception messages with information. To make limited changes to the existing exception mes- sages, follow configuration menu path SAP IMG  Production  Material Requirements Planning  Evaluation  Exception Messages  Define and Group Exception Messages. Let’s now briefly discuss the eight different exception message groups. Group 1 Exceptions An MRP run generates exception messages in group 1 when the date that was deter- mined using the opening period is in the past. For example, the start date of a planned order might be November 15. That is the date when the planned order must be con- verted into a process order so that the goods are produced on time to fulfill a demand. From this date, the system then subtracts the working days—for example, four days— from the opening period (the number of days maintained for the opening period in the scheduling margin key) and arrives at the opening date of the planned order, which in this example will be November 11. If the planned order isn’t converted into a produc- tion order after November 11, the system will display a message in this group. In other words, it’s an extra time buffer to alert the planner to convert an order proposal into a fixed supply element. Group 2 Exceptions This group contains exception messages that inform you about missing the release date for converting a purchase requisition or planned order into a purchase order or a production order, respectively. The release date can be seen in Transaction MD04. There are actually two hidden columns—one for the opening date and another for the release date. If the Start/Release Date and Opening Date columns aren’t visible in Transaction MD04, then you need to be sure to make them visible. Move the cursor so that the two lines can be seen and then drag the columns open. These columns provide valuable information about opening and conversion dates for the order proposals. The release date was calculated by subtracting the lead time from the requirements date (backward scheduling); therefore, it represents the latest date by which an order proposal (fixed, converted, a PO sent out to supplier, or a production order sent to the shop floor) has to start so that the material can be received on the required date. If this date is missed, on-time material availability might not happen, thereby causing service levels to degrade. As in group 1, an exception informs the user of a new order proposal, 03, and an excep- tion informs the user of an existing order proposal. This time, however, it’s the start (or release) date that is relevant. To address why the 03 New, and start date in the past © 747 13.13 Stock/Requirements List message is issued, you must evaluate possible lead time errors in the master data or look at the availability checking rule, which might have allowed a requirement to drop in within the replenishment lead time. It’s also possible to maintain configuration set- tings so the system switches to forward scheduling from today’s date onward if the start date falls in the past. The 06 Start date in the past message informs the user of an existing order proposal that has missed its conversion date. To address these errors, you must get all these ele- ments up to date and release them on time with the correct lead time, which will deter- mine the correct start/release date. If you need to reschedule an order proposal instead of releasing it, then check the basic data setup to see if it’s faulty and doesn’t generate the correct dates automatically. When exception 63 Production start before order start appears, it’s due to incorrect configuration settings. The system has suggested a production start date that lies before the order start date in lead time scheduling. You can fix this message by select- ing the option to adjust the basic dates in the scheduling parameters for the order pro- posals (via Transaction OPU5). Group 3 Exceptions Group 3 messages reflect a more serious problem as they not only inform you about missing the start/release date of the order but also indicate that the finish date has passed as well. With the 04 New, and finish date in the past message, the MRP run keeps trying to adjust the proposals to match supply with demand. Dates are adjusted with new order proposal creation, which creates a bullwhip effect in the planning pro- cess. You need to prioritize the exception monitoring to ensure finish dates in the past don’t happen at all or occur only minimally. The 07 Finish date in the past message is very critical because it alerts the user to an impending outage, unless there’s enough safety stock to get through the demand that’s waiting for that order to be received. Message 07 can come from a purchase req- uisition, a planned order, a PO, or a production/process order. In all cases, immediate action is warranted. Under no circumstances should there be orders in the system for which the finish date has passed. This actually means that the finish date (or the GR date, in the case of a purchase order) lies in the past. Another part of group 3 for late finishing is exception message 64 Production finish after order finish, which informs the user of an inconsistency in scheduling. The pro- duction finish, which was calculated using the routing’s lead time, lies after the basic date (calculated from the material master’s lead time). Again, this is because the basic dates aren’t adjusted—due to a setting in configuration Transaction OPU5. Group 4 Exceptions Exceptions from group 4 are general messages and are for informational purposes only to address master data or configuration inconsistencies. These exceptions can only be in Transaction MD06 (Collective MRP Lists), not in Transaction MD07 (Collective 13 Material Requirements Planning 748 Stock/Requirements Situation), because the system can’t tell when the last planning run was. This is because the dynamically created stock/requirements situation (in Transaction MD07) has no time stamp, and therefore, the system doesn’t know the new from the old. The following are some of the exception messages in group 4:  01 Newly Created Order Proposal An order proposal was newly created in the last planning run. This message is gener- ated if there is new demand in the system or when MRP runs use planning mode 3 (delete planning dates).  42 Order Proposal Has Been Changed The order proposal was changed in the planning run, either because of a change in the demand situation or because of changes made in the master data settings after the last planning run.  44 Order Proposal Re-exploded The order proposal’s BOM was re-exploded in the planning run, and new dependent requirements were created.  46 Order Proposal Has Been Manually Changed The order proposal was manually changed in the single-item planning run. Group 5 Exceptions Group 5 exception messages result from errors in the BOM explosion during the MRP run. Message 50 No BOM Exists means there is most likely no BOM for the material, or, in sales order processing, a sales order BOM could be missing. If the MRP run generates a planned order to cover demand but it can’t find a BOM suitable for the order, message 52 No BOM Selected appears. It could be that there are BOMs assigned to the material, but the selection criteria can’t assign the appropriate one to the planned order. If exception message 53 No BOM Explosion Due to Missing Config. appears, it’s due to missing configuration and customization because the line items in the BOM didn’t receive dependent requirements. Message 54 No Valid Run Schedule is an exception when using repetitive manufactur- ing. A run schedule is like a planned order, and the correct quantities couldn’t be deter- mined by the MRP run. Group 6 Exceptions Group 6 exceptions result from an availability check that evaluates stock shortages or excess stock. All messages in this group are related to quantities and stock levels. For example, message 25 Excess Stock points to the planned available stock’s coverage being greater than the maximum stock coverage specified in the range of coverage pro- file. Because the range of coverage profile is used to keep a check on minimum, target, or maximum stock levels, the MRP run checks to see inventory below the defined © 749 13.13 Stock/Requirements List levels. However, if there is a rounding value, fixed lot size, or minimum order quantity maintained in the policy, this maximum will be exceeded. For customer individual stock segments to manage individual customer stock, excep- tion 26 Shortage in Individual Segment will alert the user to higher stock levels than planned for in a range of coverage profile. When you’re using a planning time fence with fixed types (P2 or P4 in deterministic planning), message 56 No Requirements Coverage can alert you to a shortage within the planning time fence. Message 57 Disc. Matl (discontinued material) describes a situation wherein a material is partly replaced by a follow-up or replacement material used in the discontinuation process. As a planner can replace a part with a follow-up material in the discontinua- tion process, there may be a business need to receive an alert if the discontinued part was only partially replaced with the substitute material. Another exception in discon- tinuation is message 58 Uncovered Reqmt after Effective-Out Date, which is generated if a requirement exists after the effective-out date for a part that is to be discontinued and therefore can’t be covered by planned stock. And if there is a receipt—maybe from a previously generated PO—that brings in stock after the effective-out date of a discon- tinued part, exception message 59 Receipt after Effective-Out Date will appear. These are very helpful alerts that help you manage discontinuation of parts without interrup- tions, stock-outs, or leftover unconsumed stock. When using quota arrangements, a planner can source parts or materials from various vendors with an equal or unequal distribution of required quantities, called a quota. For example, a planner could order a quantity of 100 pieces for the same part from three different vendors with quotas of 40%, 35%, and 25% of the required total quantity. Should the MRP run, for whatever reason, exceed the maximum release quantity of the quota, then exception 70 Max. Release Qty—Quota Exceeded would appear. An exception message that may then appear often is 96 Stock Fallen below Safety Stock Level, which informs the user that the static safety stock set in the MRP 2 screen of the material master record is low. If you as a planner never or rarely receive this mes- sage, then the inventory level is probably too high, and all the safety stock probably turns into unused dead stock. So, it’s a good thing to receive the occasional message 96 because it means you’re making good use of the buffer without binding too much cash in inventory holdings. In addition, when a material has exception message 96, its traf- fic light turns to red, and its Days of Supply turns to –999.9, which means that all mate- rials whose safety stocks are breached can be seen at the top of the list in Transaction MD07. This might help you manage priorities and effectively address exception mes- sages. Group 7 Exceptions Four exception messages are contained in this group. One is for nonfixed order pro- posals (30), and the other three are for fixed replenishment elements, such as POs and production orders. The latter three require manual rescheduling of the orders because 13 Material Requirements Planning 750 they are fixed, and the MRP run doesn’t change them anymore. The system suggests the date to reschedule to. The four messages are explained in more detail here:  10 Bring Process Forward When a demand date or quantity has changed and a certain quantity of goods is needed at an earlier time, instead of creating another order proposal, the MRP run suggests bringing the already ordered quantities in for an earlier delivery date so they can be used to fulfill the changed demand. The rescheduling has to happen manually, and the process is often called expediting because the planner will need to reach out to the supplier to see if expediting the delivery to an earlier date (before the originally agreed upon lead time) is possible.  15 Postpone Process This message informs the user that the opposite has to happen: the ordered quanti- ties aren’t needed as early as was originally agreed to. It would be better if the sup- plier could deliver later because the demand has moved out to a later date. Not post- poning as suggested by message 15 will lead to having too much inventory too early.  20 Cancel Process This message occurs when a demand is reduced or disappears altogether. This mes- sage only appears for fixed supply elements such as a PO or a production/process order. At an earlier time, there must have been a demand causing the creation of an order proposal that must have been converted to a fixed supply order. Subse- quently, the demand must have disappeared or been reduced, but because the sup- ply was fixed, the MRP run can’t delete the order.  30 Plan Process According to Schedule The MRP run isn’t able to fulfill the demand because, according to master data or routing settings, the lead time is too long to bring the materials in on time. Group 8 Exceptions As with group 4, messages out of group 8 can’t be seen in Transaction MD07 but only in Transaction MD06. If the planning run was terminated for a material, then users see message 98 Abnormal End of Requirements Planning. This message may appear due to defective master data that prevents planning or even a prerequisite not being met, such as mandatory forecasting on the material not being performed prior to the MRP run. When you’re dealing with exception messages, the following are some of the ways you can prioritize handling them: 1. Group 8 is the most important of all the groups, so look at the abnormal ends, where the planning run aborts. Address these materials first. 2. Next, look at group 5. These concern structural problems, and the planning run can’t even come up with a date or quantity because the demand doesn’t get exploded down to the lower level. © 751 13.13 Stock/Requirements List 3. Then check out group 3. Not only was a date to firm a receipt missed, but the date when the receipt was supposed to come in is already too late to fulfill a demand. 4. After that, attend to the group 2 problems (wherein the date was missed when a pro- posal needed to be firmed) so that a planner can receive the quantity after the regu- lar lead time. If a date is missed, rescheduling and manual expediting is the only option. 5. Group 1 exceptions are only relevant while using the opening horizon to make an additional check when external procurement is triggered first by a planned order and then by a purchase requisition. 6. Therefore, you should tackle group 7 messages next. These require expediting and may take much more time to get through, but at least you can create a list at this point. You can work on the list later in the day (call vendors, check with purchasing, check the warehouse for inventory, etc.). 7. Next, deal with group 6. Inventory excess or shortages usually require a change in strategy. Again, you should make a list and see how to reduce these exceptions over time, by applying a different MRP type, changing the lot sizing procedure, looking at safety stock levels, and so on. 8. Finally, review the general messages in group 4 to see why there is a new proposal or why they have changed. These messages are informational only and don’t necessarily require action.
sections.he:
המערכת מייצרת הודעות חריגה (exception messages) ב-MRP כשהיא נתקלת בהתראות. הן מוצגות לכל אלמנט רכש ב-stock/requirements list (טור Exception, ‏Figure 13.64). ניתן גם Edit • Find in the List. האלמנטים העיקריים: עדיפות, שיוך לקבוצה, השתקה, יצירת MRP list, וטקסט. ההודעות מוצגות בעיקר בארבע טרנזקציות:
• Transaction MD04 — מצב דרישות/מלאי דינמי לחומר בודד
• Transaction MD05 — ה-MRP list (תצלום מזמן הריצה האחרונה)
• Transaction MD06 — רשימה קולקטיבית עם MRP lists
• Transaction MD07 — רשימה קולקטיבית עם מצבי stock/requirements
**Tips and Tricks:** ניתן לשנות טקסט להדגשת חשיבות (למשל "Warning: stock fallen below safety stock level"): SAP IMG • Production • Material Requirements Planning • Evaluation • Exception Messages • Define and Group Exception Messages.
שמונה קבוצות:

**קבוצה 1:** התאריך שנקבע ע"י ה-opening period בעבר. למשל, תאריך התחלת הזמנה מתוכננת ב-15/11 (תאריך ההמרה לתהליך). המערכת מחסירה ימי עבודה (4) מה-opening period → opening date 11/11. אם לא הומרה אחרי 11/11, הודעה. ‏buffer זמן נוסף להמרת הצעה לאלמנט אספקה קבוע.

**קבוצה 2:** החמצת תאריך השחרור להמרת דרישת רכש/הזמנה מתוכננת ל-PO/הזמנת ייצור. תאריך השחרור ב-Transaction MD04 (שני טורים מוסתרים — opening date ו-release date). חושב בהחסרת ה-lead time מתאריך הדרישה (backward) — התאריך האחרון שבו הצעה חייבת להתחיל. הודעות: ‏03 New, and start date in the past (הצעה חדשה — בדקו שגיאות lead time או checking rule); ‏06 Start date in the past (הצעה קיימת שהחמיצה המרה). ‏63 Production start before order start (תצורה שגויה — תזמון lead time הציע התחלה לפני ה-order start; תקנו ב-Adjust Basic Dates, ‏Transaction OPU5).

**קבוצה 3:** בעיה חמורה יותר — החמצת ה-start/release וגם תאריך הסיום עבר. ‏04 New, and finish date in the past (MRP מנסה להתאים — bullwhip effect; תעדפו ניטור). ‏07 Finish date in the past (קריטי — התראה למחסור צפוי אלא אם יש safety stock; מכל אלמנט; פעולה מיידית). ‏64 Production finish after order finish (אי-עקביות — סיום הייצור [routing lead time] אחרי ה-basic date; בשל אי-התאמת basic dates, ‏Transaction OPU5).

**קבוצה 4:** הודעות כלליות למידע (אי-עקביות נתוני אב/תצורה). רק ב-Transaction MD06 (לא MD07 — אין time stamp). למשל:
• 01 Newly Created Order Proposal (ביקוש חדש או planning mode 3)
• 42 Order Proposal Has Been Changed (שינוי ביקוש/נתוני אב)
• 44 Order Proposal Re-exploded (BOM פורק מחדש, דרישות תלויות חדשות)
• 46 Order Proposal Has Been Manually Changed

**קבוצה 5:** שגיאות בפירוק BOM. ‏50 No BOM Exists (אין BOM, או חסר sales order BOM). ‏52 No BOM Selected (יש BOMים אך הקריטריונים לא הקצו מתאים). ‏53 No BOM Explosion Due to Missing Config. (תצורה חסרה — הפריטים לא קיבלו דרישות תלויות). ‏54 No Valid Run Schedule (ב-REM — הכמויות לא נקבעו).

**קבוצה 6:** בדיקת זמינות — מחסור/עודף. ‏25 Excess Stock (הכיסוי גדול מהמקסימלי ב-range of coverage profile; rounding/אצווה קבועה/מינימום עלולים לחרוג). ‏26 Shortage in Individual Segment (מלאי לקוח). ‏56 No Requirements Coverage (מחסור בתוך ה-time fence ב-P2/P4). ‏57 Disc. Matl (חומר שהוחלף חלקית ב-follow-up). ‏58 Uncovered Reqmt after Effective-Out Date (דרישה אחרי תאריך הוצאה). ‏59 Receipt after Effective-Out Date (קבלה אחרי הוצאה). ‏70 Max. Release Qty—Quota Exceeded (חריגה ממכסה). ‏96 Stock Fallen below Safety Stock Level (ה-safety stock הסטטי נמוך; הופעה תכופה = נמוך מדי; נדירה = מלאי גבוה מדי; הפנס אדום, ‏Days of Supply = −999.9, מוצג בראש MD07).

**קבוצה 7:** ארבע הודעות. אחת להצעות לא-קבועות (30), ושלוש לאלמנטים קבועים (POs, ייצור) הדורשים תזמון-מחדש ידני (המערכת מציעה תאריך):
• 10 Bring Process Forward (זירוז/expediting — הקדמת אספקה; ידנית, פנייה לספק)
• 15 Postpone Process (דחייה — הכמויות לא נדרשות מוקדם)
• 20 Cancel Process (ביקוש פחת/נעלם; רק לאלמנטים קבועים — MRP אינו מוחק)
• 30 Plan Process According to Schedule (ה-lead time ארוך מדי)

**קבוצה 8:** כמו 4, רק ב-Transaction MD06. ‏98 Abnormal End of Requirements Planning (הריצה הופסקה — נתוני אב פגומים או תנאי לא-מולא, כגון חיזוי חובה שלא בוצע).

תיעדוף הטיפול:
1. קבוצה 8 (abnormal ends) — תחילה.
2. קבוצה 5 (בעיות מבניות — הביקוש לא פורק).
3. קבוצה 3 (החמצת firm + תאריך מאוחר מדי).
4. קבוצה 2 (החמצת תאריך firm — תזמון-מחדש ו-expediting ידני).
5. קבוצה 1 (רלוונטית רק עם opening horizon).
6. קבוצה 7 (expediting — צרו רשימה לעבודה מאוחר יותר).
7. קבוצה 6 (עודף/מחסור — שינוי אסטרטגיה: MRP type, ‏lot sizing, ‏safety stock).
8. קבוצה 4 (כללי, למידע בלבד).

sections.title: Order Report
sections.en: 13.13.4 Order Report Next, access the screen shown in Figure 13.66 via Transaction MD4C or CO46. The order report will show each element of the stock/requirements list. In this example, it shows that production order 000080000005 of main material component 25 doesn’t provide the requirements coverage, as denoted by the red traffic light. The green traffic light further down the report (not shown) represents a satisfactory stock situation, whereas the red one represents a signal for the planner to take action. Figure 13.66 Order Report 13 Material Requirements Planning 752 Note To create a custom profile that can then be used in an order report, follow menu path SAP IMG  Production Planning  Material Requirements Planning  Evaluation  Define Profiles for Order Report.
sections.he:
גשו ל-Transaction MD4C או CO46 (Figure 13.66). ה-order report מציג כל אלמנט. בדוגמה, הזמנת ייצור 000080000005 של רכיב 25 אינה מספקת כיסוי (פנס אדום). ירוק = מצב משביע-רצון; אדום = פעולה.
**הערה:** ליצירת profile מותאם: SAP IMG • Production Planning • Material Requirements Planning • Evaluation • Define Profiles for Order Report.

sections.title: Pegged Requirements
sections.en: 13.13.5 Pegged Requirements The order report finds all the receipts assigned to the requirements in a multilevel, top- down pegging overview, but it’s also possible to run a bottom-up pegging analysis to find which requirements are assigned to a given receipt element. You use Transaction MD09 to determine the pegged requirements (see Figure 13.67). Choose the Order Route and it will show the pegged requirements level by level in the lower half of the screen. Figure 13.67 Pegged Requirements
sections.he: ה-order report מוצא את כל הקבלות המוקצות לדרישות בסקירת pegging רב-רמתית top-down; אך ניתן גם ניתוח bottom-up — אילו דרישות מוקצות לקבלה. Transaction MD09 (Figure 13.67). בחרו Order Route — ה-pegged requirements רמה-אחר-רמה בחצי התחתון.

sections.title: Material Requirements Planning Elements
sections.en: 13.13.6 Material Requirements Planning Elements Because the system denotes each planning element separately, you should use the dropdown or filter function so that the system will only display the desired informa- tion (see Figure 13.68). © 753 13.13 Stock/Requirements List Figure 13.68 MRP Elements in Procurement without Requirements
sections.he: מאחר שהמערכת מציינת כל אלמנט בנפרד, השתמשו ברשימה/סינון להצגת המידע הרצוי בלבד (Figure 13.68).

sections.title: Header Details of Stock/Requirements List
sections.en: 13.13.7 Header Details of Stock/Requirements List Referring back to Figure 13.61, choose the Header Details icon to find all the parameters used by the system in planning the material. In other words, there’s no longer a need to separately view the MRP parameters in the material master; you can do so while remaining in the stock/requirements list (see Figure 13.69). Figure 13.69 Header Details 13 Material Requirements Planning 754
sections.he: ב-Figure 13.61, בחרו Header Details לכל הפרמטרים שבשימוש — אין צורך לצפות בנפרד באב החומר; ניתן תוך שהייה ברשימה (Figure 13.69).

sections.title: Interactive Conversion of Procurement Elements
sections.en: 13.13.8 Interactive Conversion of Procurement Elements When you choose the Additional Data for MRP Element icon (the magnifying glass icon on the left-hand side of the stock/requirements list) for any procurement element (e.g., a planned order), a popup appears for you to perform the interactive conversion of a planned order into either a purchase requisition for external procurement or a production/process order for in-house production.
sections.he: בבחירת Additional Data for MRP Element (זכוכית מגדלת, שמאל) לכל אלמנט רכש (כגון הזמנה מתוכננת), חלון להמרה אינטראקטיבית — לדרישת רכש (חיצוני) או הזמנת ייצור/תהליך (פנימי).

sections.title: Summation View
sections.en: 13.13.9 Summation View Figure 13.70 shows that a planner can toggle between the summation view and a detailed view of all planning elements (receipts, issuances/requirements, etc.). This icon is shown on the left-hand side of the figure (next to Individual List). Figure 13.70 Summation View of Stock Requirement List
sections.he: Figure 13.70 — ניתן לעבור בין summation view לתצוגה מפורטת של כל האלמנטים (קבלות, הנפקות/דרישות). הסמל בצד שמאל (ליד Individual List).

sections.title: Stock Statistics
sections.en: 13.13.10 Stock Statistics The screen shown in Figure 13.71 appears when you choose Goto  Stock Statistics in the stock/requirements list. The stock statistics provide comprehensive details of the stock situation of the material. The stock/requirements list also provides a complete overview of the capacity situa- tion of the in-house produced materials so that you as a planner can act or react to any unusual capacity overload in specific work centers. To view the capacity situation, nav- igate to Goto  Capacity Situation in the stock/requirements list (see Figure 13.72). © 755 13.13 Stock/Requirements List Figure 13.71 Stock Statistics Figure 13.72 Capacity Situation 13 Material Requirements Planning 756
sections.he: במסך Goto • Stock Statistics (Figure 13.71) — פרטי מצב המלאי המקיפים. הרשימה מספקת גם סקירת מצב הקיבולת של חומרים מיוצרים-פנימית — Goto • Capacity Situation (Figure 13.72) — לתגובה לעומס-יתר.

sections.title: User Settings
sections.en: 13.13.11 User Settings You can save individual display settings in the stock/requirements list to suit your preferences or business needs. Refer back to Figure 13.61: the Settings icon is available in the top-right hand side of the screen. Note We encourage you to explore the many other features and functionalities of the stock/ requirements list by choosing different icons and choosing from the menu options.
sections.he:
ניתן לשמור הגדרות תצוגה אישיות ברשימה. ב-Figure 13.61, סמל Settings בצד ימין-עליון.
**הערה:** חקרו תכונות נוספות בסמלים ובתפריט.

sections.title: Planning Calendar
sections.en: 13.14 Planning Calendar There are several instances in which either the company receives goods on specific days of the week or the supplier supplies goods only on specific days of the week. In other words, the planning of materials differs from the factory calendar of the company. For example, several agricultural products used in the production process of edible prod- ucts are produced only during specific periods of the year, and the company must pro- cure them and also store them to ensure they are available for consumption during the production process. For example, red chilies, an agricultural product, are only produced from January to April. The company uses a planning calendar to ensure the system cre- ates procurement proposals for this raw material (red chilies) within that four-month time period. It’s also possible to specify a planning date in the planning run. This option is useful because it enables a planner to bring the planning run forward to an earlier date. If the planning run is set for Monday, for example, this planning run can be performed on a Friday. The planning calendar is assigned in the MRP 2 view of the material master (Transac- tion MM02). Figure 13.73 shows the Planning Calendar field for maintaining the plan- ning calendar. Figure 13.73 Planning Calendar in Material Master © 757 13.14 Planning Calendar To create a new planning calendar, you follow menu path SAP IMG  Production  Mate- rial Requirements Planning  Master Data  Maintain Planning Calendar or use Transac- tion MD25. On the screen shown in Figure 13.74, define the Planning Calendar as “ZPP” for Plant “1710” and select the Following Working Day radio button if the period start date isn’t on a working day. Figure 13.74 Setting Up Planning Calendar Next, you define a minimum number of periods that the system must generate in the planning calendar in the Minimum Period field. When you press (Enter), a popup will appear where you can select weekdays, work weeks, workdays, work months, and so on. Next, choose the Periods button, and the New Dates popup will appear and let you define the start and end date of the planning calendar. Then, choose Continue. In Figure 13.75, notice that all period planning starts on a Monday and that this is the same as is defined in the lower half of the first screen shown in Figure 13.74. 13 Material Requirements Planning 758 Figure 13.75 Planning Calendar
sections.he:
לעיתים החברה מקבלת/הספק מספק רק בימים מסוימים — התכנון שונה מה-factory calendar. למשל, מוצרים חקלאיים מיוצרים רק בתקופות בשנה. למשל, פלפלים אדומים מיוצרים ינואר–אפריל; ה-planning calendar מבטיח שהמערכת תיצור הצעות רכש בארבעת החודשים.
ניתן גם לציין תאריך תכנון בריצה — להקדמה. אם הריצה ליום ב', ניתן להריץ ביום ו'.
ה-planning calendar מוקצה בתצוגת MRP 2 (Transaction MM02, ‏Figure 13.73).
ליצירה: SAP IMG • Production • Material Requirements Planning • Master Data • Maintain Planning Calendar, או Transaction MD25 (Figure 13.74). הגדירו Planning Calendar "ZPP" למפעל "1710", ובחרו רדיו Following Working Day אם תחילת התקופה אינה ביום עבודה. הגדירו Minimum Period; ב-Enter, חלון לבחירת ימי שבוע/שבועות עבודה/ימי עבודה/חודשי עבודה. בחרו Periods → New Dates להגדרת תחילה וסיום, ‏Continue. ב-Figure 13.75, כל התקופות מתחילות ביום ב' (כמוגדר ב-Figure 13.74).

sections.title: Planning Areas
sections.en: 13.15 Planning Areas Apart from running MRP at a single plant level, material level, or product group level, you can activate the MRP areas if you have a business need to run MRP for one of the following:  A single storage location or a group of storage locations  A subcontractor The advantage of setting up MRP areas is that you can plan materials at the storage location level, which allows planning of materials at the storage location level to be dif- ferent from MRP planning of the material at the plant level. For example, if there are consumable materials that are stored at several storage locations in a plant, then you can set the MRP type of this material to “ND” (no planning) at the plant level. However, for two specific storage locations with high consumption of this consumable material, you can set the MRP type to “VB” (reorder point planning) to ensure that the system will help to replenish this material as soon as it drops below the reorder point level in those two storage locations. MRP areas make this material planning possible. © 759 13.15 Planning Areas In this section, we show you how to configure MRP areas, activate MRP areas in the material master (including defining important planning parameters), run the MRP for MRP areas, and finally evaluate the planning run’s results. Warning You can’t deactivate MRP areas after activating them in the SAP system. Therefore, you must carefully consider whether to use MRP areas before implementing them.
sections.he:
מלבד הרצת MRP ברמת מפעל/חומר/product group, ניתן להפעיל MRP areas להרצה עבור:
• מיקום אחסון בודד או קבוצה
• subcontractor
היתרון — תכנון ברמת המיקום, שונה מהתכנון ברמת המפעל. למשל, חומר צריכה בכמה מיקומים — ‏MRP type "ND" (no planning) ברמת המפעל, אך "VB" (reorder point) לשני מיקומים בעלי צריכה גבוהה. ‏MRP areas מאפשרים זאת.
להלן: תצורה, הפעלה באב החומר, הרצה, והערכה.
**אזהרה:** אי אפשר לבטל MRP areas לאחר הפעלה — שקלו בזהירות.

sections.title: Configuration
sections.en: 13.15.1 Configuration The two main configuration steps involved in setting up MRP areas are checking the MRP Area Active box and defining the MRP areas, as described here for a storage loca- tion: 1. To activate MRP areas, you use menu path SAP IMG  Production  Material Require- ments Planning  Master Data  MRP Areas  Activate MRP for MRP Areas. Here, you check the MRP Area Active box and save. 2. To define MRP areas, use menu path SAP IMG  Production  Material Requirements Planning  Master Data  MRP Areas  Define MRP Areas for Plant/Storage Locations. 3. Then, choose New Entries, set MRP Area as “1710–171A,” and provide a description. 4. For MRP Area Type, select 02 from the dropdown menu, which is for storage location MRP. Assign the Plant as “1710” and press (Enter). 5. On the left-hand side of the screen, double-click Assign Storage Locations, which leads you to the screen shown in Figure 13.76. Note MRP area type 02 is the standard type for defining additional MRP areas on the storage location level. MRP area type 01 is for the plant MRP areas and is created automatically when you convert the planning file for MRP areas. MRP area type 03 is for subcontract- ing, in which a company’s stock is maintained at a supplier’s premises, and it ensures materials planning. 6. Assign Recg. stor. loc. (receiving storage location) as “171A” for Plant “1710” and save the entry. For this example, we used a single storage location for the plant, but you can group more than one storage location under one MRP area. This storage location (or loca- tions) will be planned separately and independently from planning at the plant level. In addition, in a subcontracting scenario involving MRP areas, you can define subcon- tracting MRP areas within a plant to enable planning and material availability at the subcontractor (supplier) level. 13 Material Requirements Planning 760 Figure 13.76 Configuring MRP Areas for Storage Location
sections.he:
שני צעדי תצורה — סימון MRP Area Active והגדרת ה-areas (למיקום אחסון):
1. להפעלה: SAP IMG • Production • Material Requirements Planning • Master Data • MRP Areas • Activate MRP for MRP Areas. סמנו MRP Area Active ושמרו.
2. להגדרה: ... • Define MRP Areas for Plant/Storage Locations.
3. בחרו New Entries, ‏MRP Area "1710–171A", ותיאור.
4. ל-MRP Area Type בחרו 02 (storage location MRP). הזינו Plant "1710", ‏Enter.
5. בשמאל, לחיצה כפולה על Assign Storage Locations (Figure 13.76).
**הערה:** סוג 02 לרמת מיקום אחסון; סוג 01 ל-plant MRP areas (נוצר אוטומטית בהמרת ה-planning file); סוג 03 ל-subcontracting (מלאי החברה אצל הספק).
6. הזינו Recg. stor. loc. "171A" למפעל "1710" ושמרו.
בדוגמה מיקום בודד, אך ניתן לקבץ מספר מיקומים תחת area אחד — מתוכננים בנפרד מהמפעל. ב-subcontracting, ניתן areas בתוך מפעל לתכנון וזמינות ברמת הספק.

sections.title: Set Up the Material Master
sections.en: 13.15.2 Set Up the Material Master With the necessary configuration settings for MRP areas in place, you can activate the storage location MRP for material 2267, plant 1710, and storage location 171A. Using Transaction MM02 for the change in the material master, you enter Material “2267” for Plant “1710,” and for Stor. Loc. 171A, you select the MRP 1 view. On the screen shown in Figure 13.77, you click the MRP Areas button so that the Create MRP Area screen shown in Figure 13.78 appears. Then, select configured MRP Area 1710–171A. Figure 13.77 MRP Areas in Material Master © 761 13.15 Planning Areas Figure 13.78 MRP Area Settings for Storage Location in Material Master Note If an error message reading MRP area 1710–171A does not exist as SCM location appears, then execute report /SAPAPO/CREATE_LOCATION for MRP area 1710-171A by using Transaction SE38. Next, assign the MRP Type as “VB” for manual reorder point planning at the MRP area level and set the Reorder Point to “200.” Then, assign other parameters, such as MRP Controller “001” and Fixed Lot Size “100.00” (not shown), per Figure 13.78. Finally, choose the MRP 2 tab. In the MRP 2 tab, more planning options are available at the material level, such as defining a Safety Stock of “70” at the MRP areas level (see Figure 13.79). Here, you should enter a Planned Deliv. Time in days and choose the Forecast tab. The Forecast tab page enables you to enter forecast parameters and also interactively execute a forecast of the material. Then, you choose the Consmptn values tab and 13 Material Requirements Planning 762 maintain the planned and unplanned consumption values. Finally, choose Adopt in the MRP areas and save the material master settings. Figure 13.79 MRP 2 Tab of MRP Area 1710–171A
sections.he:
עם התצורה, הפעילו storage location MRP לחומר 2267, מפעל 1710, מיקום 171A.
ב-Transaction MM02, הזינו Material "2267", ‏Plant "1710", ‏Stor. Loc. 171A, ובחרו תצוגת MRP 1. לחצו MRP Areas (Figure 13.77) → Create MRP Area (Figure 13.78). בחרו MRP Area 1710–171A.
**הערה:** אם מופיעה שגיאה "MRP area 1710–171A does not exist as SCM location", הריצו report /SAPAPO/CREATE_LOCATION ל-area זה ב-Transaction SE38.

Notice that Material 2267 belongs to MRP Area 1710–171A. Choose the Selected Stock/Requirements List button (not shown) to go to the screen shown in Figure 13.81, which we’ll discuss in the next section. With this report, you can copy the MRP area settings with a reference, create or change them with an MRP or forecast profile, create or change them with data, and set or reset the deletion indicator (see Figure 13.82). sections.title: Classic Material Requirements Planning
sections.en: 13.16 Classic Material Requirements Planning Now that we’ve covered MRP Live and associated business processes, let’s briefly cover the basics of classic MRP and some of the important functionality it offers. First, access the screen shown in Figure 13.83 by using Transaction MD02 to run MRP for a single material at MRP area level 1710–171A. Figure 13.83 Single-Item, Multilevel MRP (Initial Screen) The following are some of the important selection parameters of MRP:  Processing key The processing key enables the system to decide the type of planning run it needs to carry out for the material. The options for the planning run are NETCH, NETPL, and NEUPL.  Purchase requisition key If external procurement is implied, the system considers this setting during the planning run. If the necessary settings are in place, then the system can directly cre- ate purchase requisitions for all externally procured materials. Alternatively, the system can create planned orders that you can convert into purchase requisitions.  Delivery schedules If a source list for the material is maintained and the same has been incorporated into scheduling agreements with vendors, the system can create schedule lines. © 765 13.16 Classic Material Requirements Planning  Creation of MRP list The system includes the results of the planning run in the MRP list after the plan- ning run. An MRP list is a static or frozen list of stock/requirements situations, with the date and time immediately after the planning run. This indicator controls how the system should create the MRP list. The available options are for the system to create an MRP list for all planned orders, create an MRP list for planned orders with exceptions, or not create any MRP list at all. Exceptions are alerts in the system that the planner needs to keep an eye on.  Planning mode During the planning run, the system plans various procurement elements, such as unfirmed planned orders, purchase requisitions, and scheduling agreements, and it does it once again in the next planning run. You can control how the system should proceed with the planning data that is already there (from the latest planning run or due to interactive activities of the MRP planner). Three options are available: – Adopt Planning Data If there is any change in requirement quantities, dates, or lot sizing procedures for unfirmed planned orders (or other procurement elements), the system re- explodes the BOM for the new quantities in the MRP run. – Re-explode BOM and Routing The system re-explodes the BOM and routing if there is a change in the BOM mas- ter data, routing, production versions, or BOM explosion numbers. This helps to ensure that the system re-explodes the BOM for the existing unfirmed planned orders. The procurement proposals created in the previous planning aren’t deleted but are adjusted to take the changes into account. – Delete and Recreate Planning data The system deletes the existing procurement proposals (i.e., the entire planning data of the previous planning run), unless they are firmed, and it re-explodes the BOM and routing, thereby creating altogether new procurement proposals.  Scheduling types For in-house-produced materials, the system offers two types of scheduling options: – Basic date scheduling – Lead time scheduling After you enter the parameters on the initial screen of Transaction MD02, press (Enter) twice (first to confirm the MRP parameters, causing the entered parameters to turn red, and then to execute the MRP run) and the system will bring up the plan- ning result screen for a large number of materials. On this result screen, not only the finished or semifinished goods (2267) are planned but also all the components of the BOM. You can view the planning result of a material by double-clicking it. 13 Material Requirements Planning 766

כעת יסודות ה-MRP הקלאסי. גשו ל-Transaction MD02 להרצת MRP לחומר בודד ברמת MRP area 1710–171A (Figure 13.83). פרמטרי בחירה חשובים:
• **Processing key:** קובע את סוג הריצה — NETCH, ‏NETPL, ‏NEUPL.
• **Purchase requisition key:** ברכש חיצוני, המערכת יכולה ליצור דרישות רכש ישירות, או הזמנות מתוכננות להמרה.
• **Delivery schedules:** אם source list מתוחזק ומשולב ב-scheduling agreements, המערכת יוצרת schedule lines.
• **Creation of MRP list:** ה-MRP list הוא רשימה סטטית/קפואה של מצבי stock/requirements בזמן הריצה. אפשרויות: ליצור לכל ההזמנות, רק עם חריגות, או כלל לא.
• **Planning mode:** כיצד לטפל בנתוני התכנון הקיימים:
  – **Adopt Planning Data:** בשינוי כמויות/תאריכים/lot sizing להזמנות לא-קבועות, המערכת מפרקת מחדש את ה-BOM לכמויות החדשות.
  – **Re-explode BOM and Routing:** בשינוי נתוני אב BOM/routing/גרסאות/BOM explosion numbers — פירוק מחדש להזמנות לא-קבועות; ההצעות הקודמות אינן נמחקות אלא מותאמות.
  – **Delete and Recreate Planning data:** מחיקת ההצעות הקיימות (כל נתוני התכנון, פרט למקובעות), פירוק מחדש, ויצירת הצעות חדשות לחלוטין.
• **Scheduling types:** לייצור פנימי — basic date או lead time scheduling.
לאחר הזנת הפרמטרים (MD02), ‏Enter פעמיים (אישור הפרמטרים — הופכים לאדומים; ואז ביצוע). מתוכננים הגמורים/חצי-גמורים (2267) וכל רכיבי ה-BOM. לחיצה כפולה על חומר מציגה את תוצאתו.

sections.title: Types of Planning Runs
sections.en: 13.17 Types of Planning Runs Depending on the business process, a planner can use one of several types of planning run available in the SAP S/4HANA system. A planning run denotes the level and mode at which a planner wants to run MRP. For example, a planner may want to run MRP on an individual plant or a group of plants, on an individual material or a group of materi- als (product group), in online mode, or in background mode. Some of the planning runs include the following:  Total planning online  Total planning background  Single-item planning, sales order  Single-item planning, project We discuss each of the planning runs in the following sections.
sections.he:
לפי התהליך, ניתן לבחור סוג ריצה — הרמה והמצב להרצת MRP. למשל, מפעל בודד או קבוצה, חומר בודד או product group, online או רקע. חלק מהסוגים:
• Total planning online
• Total planning background
• Single-item planning, sales order
• Single-item planning, project

sections.title: Total Planning Online
sections.en: 13.17.1 Total Planning Online In this type of planning run, the system carries out a multilevel planning run—that is, for all the materials in a plant, for all the materials in multiple plants, or for MRP, as defined through Scope of Planning, which is available on the selection screen. Total planning online is carried out using Transaction MD01. If the business process requires you to consider and use other parameters in the MRP run, then you can either define them or use a user exit. For example, if your company wants to carry out the MRP run for a set of MRP controllers only or for a specific pro- curement type (E: In-house managed, F: Externally procured, X: Both), then you should use a user exit. The user exit enhancement is M61X00001, and we recommend that you to engage an ABAP consultant for this.
sections.he:
המערכת מבצעת ריצה רב-רמתית — לכל החומרים במפעל, במספר מפעלים, או לפי Scope of Planning. מבוצע ב-Transaction MD01.
אם נדרשים פרמטרים נוספים, הגדירו או השתמשו ב-user exit. למשל, להרצה לקבוצת MRP controllers או procurement type ספציפי (E: פנימי, F: חיצוני, X: שניהם) — השתמשו ב-user exit. ההרחבה M61X00001 (ערבו ABAP).

sections.title: Total Planning Background
sections.en: 13.17.2 Total Planning Background With the total planning background method, you can carry out the planning in the background, as opposed to in the foreground or online. Using Transaction MDBT, you can create a variant of the Transaction MD01N screen and schedule it in the back- ground on a periodic basis. The program name for Transaction MDBT is RMMRP000. Use Transaction SE38, give the program name, and define the variant to execute the MRP in the background.
sections.he: ב-total planning background, התכנון ברקע (לא online). ב-Transaction MDBT, צרו variant של מסך MD01N ותזמנו ברקע תקופתית. שם התוכנית ל-MDBT הוא RMMRP000. ב-Transaction SE38, הזינו את שם התוכנית והגדירו את ה-variant.

sections.title: Single-Item Planning, Sales Order
sections.en: 13.17.3 Single-Item Planning, Sales Order For MTO production, you can use single-item planning for a sales order. Enter the sales order number together with the line item of the sales order and use Transaction MD50 © 767
sections.he: ל-MTO, השתמשו בתכנון פריט-בודד להזמנת מכירה. הזינו מספר הזמנה ושורת פריט, והשתמשו ב-Transaction MD50.

sections.title: Summary
sections.en: 13.18 Summary to execute the planning. The system not only creates a procurement element or receipt with the sales order reference for the finished good but also plans all the components defined in the BOM of the finished good.
sections.he: המערכת יוצרת אלמנט רכש/קבלה עם הפניית הזמנת המכירה למוצר הגמור, ומתכננת את כל הרכיבים ב-BOM.

sections.title: Single-Item Planning, Project
sections.en: 13.17.4 Single-Item Planning, Project You can also execute separate planning for ETO materials. If the material—a finished good or a spare part for a raw material—is assigned to a WBS element, then use Trans- action MD51 to execute planning. Note Materials planning is a very complex topic and requires you to have a much deeper understanding of how to formulate material planning rules and policies in a company that can then be mapped in the SAP system. Here, we recommend that you read Mate- rial Requirements Planning with SAP S/4HANA (www.sap-press.com/5861, SAP PRESS, 2024), which discuss this topic in great detail. 13.18 Summary A company can take enormous advantage of the MRP functionality in the SAP S/4HANA system to help it improve and optimize its business processes. A planner can plan all types of materials, including high-, medium-, and low-value materials. The various lot- sizing procedures and safety stocks ensure that there’s neither an overstock nor a stock-out situation. The planning calendar helps a planner plan materials that are spe- cific to particular calendars only. This chapter focused on some of the latest planning innovations available in SAP S/4HANA. MRP Live provides far more options for improved planning and scheduling of materials and capacity, and MRP areas can be implemented to plan materials at the storage location or subcontracting supplier level. The next chapter covers demand-driven replenishment (DDR) in SAP S/4HANA. ©
sections.he:
ניתן לתכנן בנפרד חומרי ETO. אם החומר (גמור או חלף) מוקצה ל-WBS element, השתמשו ב-Transaction MD51.
**הערה:** תכנון חומרים מורכב ודורש הבנה עמוקה. מומלץ Material Requirements Planning with SAP S/4HANA ‏(www.sap-press.com/5861, ‏SAP PRESS, 2024).
**13.18 סיכום:** ניתן לנצל את MRP בהרחבה. ניתן לתכנן כל סוג חומר (ערך גבוה/בינוני/נמוך). שיטות ה-lot-sizing ו-safety stocks מבטיחות לא עודף ולא אזילה. ה-planning calendar מסייע לחומרים ספציפיים-לוח. הפרק התמקד בחידושים — ‏MRP Live (יותר אפשרויות לתכנון ותזמון), ו-MRP areas (תכנון ברמת מיקום/ספק subcontracting). הפרק הבא — demand-driven replenishment (DDR).

sections.title: Limitations of Current Materials Planning and
sections.en: 14.1 Limitations of Current Materials Planning and Replenishment Tools Let’s first evaluate why traditional materials planning tools are falling short of address- ing the challenges of the VUCA world. It’s important for you to understand that while many of these planning tools effectively work in isolation, they can’t work cohesively enough to reduce or eliminate the bullwhip effect. And as we evaluate each material planning tool to explain why it’s falling short, it’s equally important for you to under- stand that implementing a DDR solution doesn’t entail discarding all these planning tools, such as forecasting, MRP, safety stock, and reorder point planning. Rather, it requires you to use selected and effective features of several of these planning tools to improve the flow of materials and relevant information. For example, DDR still uses MRP for quantity calculation and scheduling of components, but it stops at stocked or buffered positions. In contrast, MRP starts at the lowest level of a BOM, which is often the highest level of the product (e.g., a finished product), and it continues quantity cal- culation and scheduling of all components of the BOM until it reaches the highest level of a BOM (often the raw materials and packing materials). Similarly, the forecasting tool is still a required planning tool in the overall context of using DDR, as is using capacity requirements planning tools in the context of overall supply chain planning. Bullwhip Effect The bullwhip effect is a cascading and incremental increase in the logistics and supply chain’s variability as a result of a small change in customer demand. The most important material planning tools and their current limitations are as fol- lows:  Forecasting Forecasting uses historical data to predict or forecast future requirements and uses forecasting models, such as constant, moving average, seasonal, and trend. All fore- casts also have a degree of error to account for deviations (mean average deviations) between forecast figures and the confidence in these figures. However, forecasts start out wrong, and they are riddled with errors that only increase with time. Fore- casts are also more inaccurate when they are made at the individual stock-keeping unit level. Imagine trying to accurately forecast or predict the number of air condi- tioners of a specific model (individual stock-keeping units) to produce a year from © 771 14.1 Limitations of Current Materials Planning and Replenishment Tools now (over a long-term horizon) when there just isn’t enough information available now and predicting how hot the weather is going to be a year from now is unreliable.  Sales and operations planning (S&OP) Forecasting often forms the basis of S&OP. A sales and operations plan ensures that the annual sales plan matches up with the production (operations) plan. The mutually agreed-upon sales and operations plan then enables a company to evaluate the ware- house space, the machines’ capacities, and the procurement commitment (value) it will need for the entire year. However, when inaccurate forecasting forms the basis of S&OP, sales and production plans are most certainly bound to change over the near- term horizon when actual sales and demand are better known.  Demand management Demand management is the last step for a materials planner to check and validate a sales or production plan to use for production and procurement planning by using the master production scheduling and MRP tools. (The plan is driven by the S&OP of the previous step.) The basis of demand management is an unreliable forecast, which leads to precisely wrong procurement and proposals generation.  Master production scheduling (MPS) An MPS program plans and schedules production of critical materials and ensures that there are no changes to the production plan within the defined time horizon, such as within a week. No changes are made to the master production scheduling after an MRP run. MPS runs before MRP so that critical products and components are planned first in the planning process. As the demand management plan is fed into MPS, it’s clear to see why MPS only adds to the supply chain chaos.  Material requirements planning (MRP) MRP explodes the BOMs of finished products to calculate the quantities of the semi- finished, packing, and raw materials required to produce finished products.  Materials planning using safety stock Safety stock is the buffer stock of materials that planners turn to in case of a sudden and unforeseen demand spike or a supply disruption. Although it’s possible to auto- matically calculate safety stock, safety stock is unable to account for the dynamic nature of supply and demand variabilities. Furthermore, the safety stock calculation method isn’t the primary materials planning tool and therefore cannot truly act as a buffer between demand and supply deviations.  Reorder point planning When stock falls below a reorder point, replenishment is triggered. The replenish- ment’s proposal quantity is often a fixed or minimum lot that’s intended to prevent the ERP system from creating an unnecessarily large number of procurement pro- posals of small quantities each time there’s a material shortage (or when a material’s stock falls below the reorder point). As with safety stock, you can calculate the reorder point of a material automatically; however, reorder point planning can’t reflect the replenishment priorities of different materials. 14 Demand-Driven Replenishment 772
sections.he:
תחילה — מדוע כלי התכנון המסורתיים אינם מתמודדים עם אתגרי עולם ה-VUCA. רבים מהם עובדים בבידוד אך אינם מסוגלים לעבוד יחד מספיק להפחתת ה-bullwhip effect. יישום DDR אינו זונח את הכלים (חיזוי, MRP, ‏safety stock, ‏reorder point) — אלא משתמש בתכונות נבחרות שלהם לשיפור זרימת החומרים והמידע. למשל, DDR עדיין משתמש ב-MRP לחישוב כמויות ותזמון רכיבים, אך עוצר ב-stocked/buffered positions. בניגוד לכך, MRP מתחיל מהרמה הנמוכה של ה-BOM וממשיך עד הגבוהה (גלם ואריזה). גם החיזוי ו-capacity requirements planning נדרשים בהקשר הכולל.
**ה-Bullwhip Effect:** עלייה מדורגת והולכת בשונות שרשרת האספקה כתוצאה משינוי קטן בביקוש הלקוח.
הכלים ומגבלותיהם:
• **Forecasting:** משתמש בהיסטוריה לחיזוי, במודלים (constant, ‏moving average, ‏seasonal, ‏trend). לכל חיזוי דרגת שגיאה (MAD) שגדלה עם הזמן. מדויק פחות ברמת stock-keeping unit בודד. (לדמיין חיזוי מזגנים של דגם ספציפי לשנה קדימה.)
• **S&OP:** מבוסס לרוב על חיזוי. מתאים את תוכנית המכירות לייצור — להערכת שטח, קיבולת, ומחויבות רכש. אך חיזוי לא-מדויק כבסיס → תוכניות משתנות.
• **Demand Management:** הצעד האחרון לבדיקת התוכנית לפני MPS ו-MRP. הבסיס — חיזוי לא-אמין → הצעות שגויות במדויק.
• **MPS:** מתכנן ומתזמן חומרים קריטיים ומבטיח אי-שינוי באופק (שבוע). רץ לפני MRP. מאחר שתוכנית ה-demand management מוזנת אליו — מוסיף לכאוס.
• **MRP:** מפרק BOMים לחישוב כמויות חצי-גמורים, אריזה וגלם.
• **Safety stock:** buffer לספייק/שיבוש. ניתן לחישוב אוטומטי, אך אינו מתמודד עם הטבע הדינמי של השונות, ואינו הכלי הראשי.
• **Reorder point:** חידוש בנפילה מתחת לנקודה. הכמות לרוב אצווה קבועה/מינימלית. ניתן לחישוב אוטומטי, אך אינו משקף עדיפויות חידוש שונות.

sections.title: Material and Information Flows
sections.en: 14.2 Material and Information Flows According to George W. Plossl, author of Production and Inventory Control: Principles and Techniques (Prentice Hall, 1967), “All benefits will be directly related to the speed of flow of information and materials.” Now more than ever, we can enhance this concept by adding that the flow of materials and information must be relevant to the required out-of-market information because in today’s hyperconnected world, companies are drowning in data but starving for relevant information to help them navigate the VUCA challenges of the modern supply chain. Furthermore, the words all benefits can be broken down into the following benefits or KPIs that companies seek to achieve:  Exceptional customer service ensures timely and quality products.  Revenue increases or at least remains stable.  The quality of products and services keeps getting better.  Inventories of purchased, WIP, and produced products stay at optimal levels.  Expenses remain minimal by eliminating expedited freight costs, rework, and unplanned partial deliveries.  Cash flow is greatly improved. With these points in mind, it’s critically important for you to address distortions lead- ing to relevant information or material flows as often and as soon as possible to create a smoother supply chain. First, let’s look at why distortions of relevant material and information occur, as illus- trated in Figure 14.1. Starting at the bottom of Figure 14.1, materials planners use MRP 1 to calculate future demand for products to ensure timely production and procure- ment. However, due to its inherent logic, MRP treats everything as dependent and acts as one big calculator to suggest production and procurement quantities of materials on specific dates. In today’s complex and globalized supply chain, the time it takes to pro- cure and produce a product is much longer than it has ever been before. At the same time, customers today have far more options to choose from, and that leads to shrink- ing customer tolerance time for a company to deliver or ensure availability of a prod- uct 2. To better predict customer demand and feed that data into the MRP program, compa- nies use forecasting tools 3. Unfortunately, even the best forecasting model or pro- gram always has a degree of error. The longer the forecast horizon is—such as yearly, quarterly, or even monthly—the greater the degree of error 4. The more detailed the level at which forecasting is done, such as at the individual product or stock keeping unit level, the more amplified the forecasting error, which leads to the distortion of rel- evant information 8. Refer again to the bottom of Figure 14.1. While MRP uses forecasting to predict demand 3, when the actual customers’ demand is known, adjustment between forecasted demand and actual demand must happen 5, and that leads to nervousness 6 in the © 773 14.2 Material and Information Flows logistics and supply chain. These conflicting and often-changing demand signals 7 again lead to the distortion of relevant information 8. Using distorted or unreliable information for materials planning is one of the two major reasons for the bullwhip effect, which is the amplification of supply variability as the result of demand variability and which has cascading and negative ripple effects on the supply chain. The second effect of nervousness 6 is that companies often use materials planning, such as production or procurement planning with time horizons of one-week or even two-week buckets 9, to bring some sanity to production or procurement plans and to prevent frequent changes to these plans. In doing so, planners use latent signals j that again result in the distortion of relevant information 8. The third factor that adds nervousness 6 to the supply chain appears when materials planners attempt to flatten BOMs k to reduce material quantities or scheduling vari- abilities. In doing so, materials planners end up using oversimplified signals l for pro- curement or production planning, which further adds to the distortion of relevant information 8. When distorted information is used, it’s no surprise that the products or materials required aren’t ready or available when needed m, and that eventually cul- minates in the distortion of relevant materials n. When relevant materials are dis- torted, companies either end up with products that don’t sell (which is an overstock scenario) or with no products to deliver on time to meet demand (which is an out-of- stock scenario); both scenarios lead to missed business opportunities and lost custom- ers. Let’s now go back again to the bottom of Figure 14.1 to understand how the MRP pro- gram that treats all materials as dependent 1 leads to the same distortions of relevant materials n created by nervousness 6 in the supply chain previously. Just like a big cal- culator, the MRP program performs a level-by-level explosion of BOMs of finished goods to calculate the quantities of semifinished, packing, and raw materials that are required at specific times; the resultant MRP plans of quantities and schedules are based on all these dependencies o. Because the MRP program is designed to ensure that the quantities of all materials in a BOM eventually net to zero after taking any safety stock into account, any change in plans, variability, or disruption on the supply side has multiplying effects on all dependent requirements, leading to the accumula- tion of delays p. The delays accumulate, but the gains do not, and thus, material plan- ners have MRP-generated production and procurement plans that are never properly synchronized q between demand and supply. The end results are the same as before: companies end up with overstock of slow-moving products or products that don’t sell, while stock-outs occur for high-demand products. In the following sections, we’ll look at how decoupling can serve as a solution to this problem, and we’ll also cover the basics of demand-driven material requirements plan- ning (DDMRP) and its components. 14 Demand-Driven Replenishment 774 Figure 14.1 Information and Material Distortions (©Demand Driven Institute, Used with Permission)

לפי George W. Plossl (Production and Inventory Control, ‏Prentice Hall, 1967): "כל היתרונות קשורים ישירות למהירות זרימת המידע והחומרים." כיום, יש להוסיף שזרימת החומרים והמידע חייבת להיות רלוונטית — חברות טובעות בנתונים אך רעבות למידע רלוונטי. "כל היתרונות" = KPIs:
• שירות לקוח יוצא-דופן (מוצרים בזמן ובאיכות).
• הכנסות עולות או יציבות.
• איכות מוצרים ושירותים משתפרת.
• מלאי (נרכש, WIP, מיוצר) ברמות אופטימליות.
• הוצאות מינימליות (ביטול משלוחי דחיפה, rework, אספקות חלקיות).
• תזרים מזומנים משופר.
יש לטפל בעיוותים בזרימת המידע/החומרים בהקדם. (Figure 14.1 — עיוותים:) ‏(1) מתכננים משתמשים ב-MRP לחישוב ביקוש עתידי, אך הוא מתייחס להכל כתלוי ופועל כמחשבון אחד גדול. ‏(2) זמן הרכש והייצור ארוך מתמיד, וזמן הסבילות של הלקוח מצטמצם. ‏(3) חברות משתמשות בחיזוי להזנת MRP. ‏(4) ככל שהאופק ארוך, השגיאה גדולה יותר; ‏(8) ככל שהרמה מפורטת (SKU בודד), השגיאה מתעצמת → עיוות מידע. ‏(5) בידיעת הביקוש בפועל, נדרשת התאמה לחיזוי → ‏(6) עצבנות (nervousness) → ‏(7) אותות מתחלפים וסותרים → ‏(8) עיוות. שימוש במידע מעוות הוא אחת משתי הסיבות העיקריות ל-bullwhip effect.
האפקט השני של העצבנות (6) — שימוש בתכנון ב-buckets של שבוע/שבועיים (9) למניעת שינויים תכופים, תוך שימוש ב-latent signals (10) → עיוות (8). הגורם השלישי — ניסיון להשטיח BOMים (11) → oversimplified signals (12) → עיוות (8). כשמשתמשים במידע מעוות, המוצרים אינם זמינים בזמן (13) → עיוות חומרים רלוונטיים (14) → עודף (מוצרים שלא נמכרים) או חוסר (אין לספק) — הזדמנויות אבודות ולקוחות אבודים.
ה-MRP (המתייחס להכל כתלוי, 1) מוביל לאותם עיוותים: פירוק רמה-אחר-רמה של BOMים מבוסס על כל התלויות (15). מאחר שהוא מתוכנן שהכל ינטרל לאפס (לאחר safety stock), כל שינוי/שיבוש בצד ההיצע מתרבה על כל הדרישות התלויות → הצטברות עיכובים (16). העיכובים מצטברים אך הרווחים לא, והתוכניות לעולם אינן מסונכרנות (17) בין ביקוש להיצע — שוב עודף ל-slow-moving וחוסר ל-high-demand.
להלן: decoupling כפתרון, ויסודות DDMRP ורכיביו.

sections.title: Demand-Driven Material Requirements Planning Basics and
sections.en: 14.3 Demand-Driven Material Requirements Planning Basics and Components The solution to the distortion of relevant information and the quagmire of material flows lies in decoupling the logistics and supply chains to reduce the bullwhip effect. Decoupling entails disconnecting the ever-present and constantly increasing variabil- ity between demand and supply by placing buffers at strategic points, known as decou- pling points. Materials planners then regularly monitor the buffers in the material value chain—from procurement to interplant transfer to production to distribution— to ensure timely action and interventions where necessary. There are three types of buffers: Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Why? Distortions to relevant materials Distortions to relevant information Material is not ready at needed time Signals with known errors are used Latent signals are used Oversimplified signals are used Supply variability transference causes delay accumulation across dependent networks Cumulative Manufacturing and Procurement Times are much longer than customer tolerance times MRP Plans (timing and quantity requirements) are built using all dependencies MRP treats everything as dependent Weekly buckets are used BOMs are flattened Changing and conflicting signals MRP Plans never properly synchronize Adjustments must occur as actual demand becomes known MRP is loaded with forecasts Nervousness © 775 14.3 Demand-Driven Material Requirements Planning Basics and Components 1. Stock buffer The stock situation at each buffer is closely monitored to ensure that there’s no shortage of the required materials. The icon denotes a decoupled position and maintains a stock buffer in DDR. 2. Time buffer This buffer manages demand and supply variability that may impact production or procurement scheduling. The time buffer icons are these: 3. Capacity buffer This buffer at production lines or work centers provides the cushions required for smoother flow to in-house-produced materials. The capacity buffer icons are these: The three color codes represent different buffer statuses: red points the materials plan- ners to areas that need immediate attention or urgent action, yellow requires closely monitoring the buffer situation, and green reflects a comfortable buffer situation. Each color of buffer is also accompanied by a percentage to denote the buffer remaining or unconsumed in relation to the overall buffer size. For example, a work center, such as a tablet-packing line, might show a red color in the tricolor buffer status to indicate 12% remaining (unconsumed) capacity. All reports and metrics used to represent buffers show red at the top (or highest) level to reflect the criticality or severity of the buffer sit- uation, while green gets the lowest position. Exceptional situations such as stock-outs, overstocks, and overcapacities are denoted by different colors, such as deep red for stock-outs or overcapacities and deep blue for overstocks or excess available capacities. As this chapter will discuss later, these deep-red and dark-blue zones are often the best candidates for bringing improvements to material and information flows. Note SAP introduced DDR in SAP S/4HANA Cloud 1708 and SAP S/4HANA 1709. DDR is based on the DDMRP methodology from the Demand Driven Institute (DDI). Carol Ptak and Chad Smith, partners at DDI, have committed themselves to promoting and proliferat- ing DDMRP and associated concepts and working throughout the world. In their book DDMRP: Demand Driven Materials Requirement Planning (3rd edition, Industrial Press, 2019), Ptak and Smith provide a deep dive into and authoritative resources on DDMRP and associated concepts. Figure 14.2 shows an example planning screen for DDR with several parts, with varying priorities denoted by corresponding tricolor buffer statuses. Figure 14.3 represents the supply chain. Starting from the left, a buffer is placed at the decoupling point 1, which is between the component manufacturing and subassem- bly steps. Notice the reduction in the variability wave 2 that dampens the bullwhip effect and also notice the associated lead time reduction 3. 14 Demand-Driven Replenishment 776 Figure 14.2 Example of DDR Planning Screen (©Demand Driven Institute, Used with Permis- sion) Figure 14.3 Decoupling to Reduce Bullwhip Effect (©Demand Driven Institute, Used with Permission) In the following sections, we’ll discuss not only where to implement DDR in the logis- tics and supply chain but also the five main components of DDMRP.
sections.he:
הפתרון לעיוות המידע וזרימת החומרים — decoupling (ניתוק) של השרשראות להפחתת ה-bullwhip effect. ‏Decoupling = ניתוק השונות ההולכת וגדלה בין ביקוש להיצע ע"י הצבת buffers בנקודות אסטרטגיות (decoupling points). המתכננים מנטרים את ה-buffers בשרשרת — מרכש לבין-מפעלי לייצור להפצה — לפעולה בזמן. שלושה סוגי buffers:
1. **Stock buffer:** מצב המלאי בכל buffer מנוטר למניעת מחסור. הסמל מציין decoupled position עם stock buffer.
2. **Time buffer:** מנהל שונות ביקוש/היצע המשפיעה על תזמון.
3. **Capacity buffer:** בקווים/מרכזים — כרית לזרימה חלקה לחומרים פנימיים.
שלושה צבעים: אדום — דורש פעולה דחופה; צהוב — ניטור צמוד; ירוק — מצב נוח. כל buffer מלווה באחוז (הנותר/הלא-נצרך). דוחות מציגים אדום בראש (חומרה), ירוק בתחתית. מצבים חריגים — stock-outs/overcapacities (אדום כהה), ‏overstocks (כחול כהה) — מועמדים לשיפור.
**הערה:** SAP הכניסה DDR ב-S/4HANA Cloud 1708 ו-S/4HANA 1709, מבוסס מתודולוגיית DDMRP מ-Demand Driven Institute (DDI). ‏Carol Ptak ו-Chad Smith (DDMRP, מהדורה 3, ‏Industrial Press, 2019).
Figure 14.2 — מסך תכנון DDR עם חלקים בעדיפויות לפי buffer tricolor. ‏Figure 14.3 — שרשרת אספקה: ‏(1) buffer ב-decoupling point בין ייצור רכיב לתת-הרכבה; ‏(2) הפחתת גל השונות; ‏(3) הפחתת lead time.

Purchasing Purchased parts often experience supply variability. 2. Operations Production operations that produce several common parts and work centers with bottleneck capacities are the prime candidates for DDR. For semifinished goods sold by a company directly to its customers, implementing DDR can mitigate the risks of demand variability due to customers’ changing requirements for the company’s products. 3. Distribution Finished goods or even services’ spare parts are distributed to different distribution centers and experience significant demand variability. 4. Interplant Companies with several manufacturing units or warehouses spread across various locations of a country, different countries, or even continents have materials with short, medium, or long lead times. Due to the special procurement types of such materials, some of them are prime candidates for DDR.

1. **Purchasing:** חלקים נרכשים סובלים משונות היצע.
2. **Operations:** פעולות המייצרות חלקים משותפים ומרכזי בקבוק — מועמדים מובהקים. לחצי-גמורים הנמכרים ישירות, ‏DDR ממתן סיכוני שונות ביקוש.
