המפתח להצלחה — הגנה וקידום זרימת חומר ומידע רלוונטיים, באמצעות מדדים (KPIs) ואנליטיקה. שלושה גורמים: אמינות אות הביקוש, יציבות, ומהירות. תחילה מדדי המפתח.
**מדדי מפתח:** DDMRP דורש buffers בנקודות אסטרטגיות לתכנון/תזמון/ביצוע עצמאיים — inventory positioning. גם כמה מלאי — inventory sizing. שניהם מובילים ליתרונות (הפחתת הון חוזר, עלויות אחסון, עלויות זירוז) ושיפור יעילות הייצור.
**Inventory Positioning:** ייצוג גרפי של מצב המלאי — ציר-x זמן, ציר-y מלאי. הקו המקווקו השחור — סדרת החידוש. חשוב לזהות חדירות עמוקות לאזורי האזהרה (צהוב, אדום). שורשי הבעיה: המתכנן איחר בחידוש, משלוח התעכב, או תקלת ייצור. חברות מעריכות ספקים לפי מספר ה-stock-outs, אורך העיכובים, וכמה חומרי-הורה הושפעו. Figure 14.48 — מדדי stock buffers (שמאל) ו-capacity buffers (ימין); הקווים המקווקווים — מצבים להערכה (understock, ‏overstock, קיבולת). מומלץ להעריך על-פני אופק ארוך (מגמה רחבה, לא עיכוב חד-פעמי).
**Inventory Sizing:** הערכת קבוצת חומרים בעלי מאפיינים דומים (lead time ארוך, אותו ספק, בקבוק קיבולת) נותנת תובנות רבות יותר. שלבים: ‏Stage 1 — התפלגות דו-מודלית עם חדירות עמוקות (stock-out ו-overstock); ‏Stage 2 — יישום DDR, שיפור ניכר אך עדיין outliers; ‏Stage 3 — שיפורים נוספים (מקורות חלופיים יקרים אך מהירים) → ביטול ה-outliers.
**גורמים המשפיעים על DDR:**
• **Signal integrity:** האם יש תקשורת מלאה, נכונה ובזמן של הנתונים לחידוש בזמן — מדד למהירות תגובת המערכת/המתכננים לאותות. הערכה בהשוואת ה-net flow position היומי ל-TOG (להמלצה, לא לביצוע). החידוש צריך להיות בזמן ובכמות המומלצת; איחור/אי-התאמה → שחיקת buffer.
• **Decoupling point integrity:** ‏decoupling point הוא מלאי עצמאי הסופג שונות. להבטחת אמינותו, יש להעריך תמיד את סיבות הסטיות בזרימה. באנליטיקה, מזהים חומרים עם שונות גדולה בין מתוכנן לבפועל. משווים את ערך המלאי ל-TOY (אזור הביצוע) → סטטוס באחוז.
• **Decoupling point velocity:** מדד תדירות ההזמנות המתוכננות והבפועל — order frequency variance. למשל, תוכנן 10 הזמנות חודשיות אך בוצעו 5,616 — סטייה המצביעה על צורך בהגדלת תדירות. קבוצת חומרים נמדדת ל-flow index (תדירות מול ADU). חשוב גם להעריך חומרים המוזמנים בתדירות גבוהה מאוד (מסווים את המהירות בפועל).

sections.title: Summary
sections.en: 14.6 Summary for improvement in materials flow. With analytics, you can monitor such critical material flow metrics and take action to improve the flow index. 14.6 Summary DDR shifts the entire paradigm from the “supply” side of planning to the “demand” side, wherein only the materials in demand are procured and produced to reduce stock- outs and overstock situations. This chapter covered the necessary DDR configuration and master data setup, and it then reviewed a few relevant transactions to accurately and correctly reflect them in the DDR business processes. The DDR business processes consist of classifying products, positioning buffers, and calculating buffers. We also dis- cussed the planning and execution steps of DDR. The next chapter covers predictive material requirements planning (pMRP), which is an innovative materials and capacity planning simulation tool that can help you improve your logistics and supply chain management. ©
sections.he: DDR מעביר את הפרדיגמה מצד ה-"supply" לצד ה-"demand" — רק חומרים בביקוש נרכשים ומיוצרים, להפחתת stock-outs ו-overstock. הפרק כיסה תצורה ונתוני אב, טרנזקציות רלוונטיות, והתהליכים (סיווג מוצרים, מיקום buffers, חישוב buffers), וצעדי התכנון והביצוע. הפרק הבא — predictive MRP (pMRP), כלי סימולציה לתכנון חומרים וקיבולת.

sections.title: Basics
sections.en: 15.1 Basics The pMRP functionality doesn’t require any configuration settings at all. This means that you can use pMRP right away as long as the proper operational MRP configuration is in place, such as a valid plant, MRP controllers, and so on. The pMRP functionality does, however, need the following basic master data and transactional data to already be in place:  Material master Any MRP-relevant material can be used for a pMRP simulation. Define scenario Create simulation Adjust simulation Analyze Process simulation Copy and simplify master data = reference data Implement changes to operations © 839
sections.he:
פונקציונליות pMRP אינה דורשת תצורה כלל — ניתן להשתמש בה מיד כל עוד יש תצורת MRP תפעולית תקינה (מפעל תקף, ‏MRP controllers וכו'). ‏pMRP דורש שנתוני האב והטרנזקציה הבאים כבר קיימים:
• **אב חומר:** כל חומר רלוונטי-MRP שמיש לסימולציה.
(זרימת התהליך: Define scenario → Create simulation → Process simulation → Adjust simulation → Analyze → Implement changes to operations; ‏Copy and simplify master data = reference data.)

sections.title: Setup
sections.en: 15.2 Setup  BOM A valid BOM with the BOM usage set to 1—Production should exist for a material that will be used in a simulation.  Work center The work center used in a simulation should have at least one capacity relevant for finite scheduling.  Routing A valid routing should exist, and the operation in the bottleneck resource operation should be relevant to capacity planning.  Production version At least one valid production version referring to the BOM and routing should exist. If there is more than one valid production version, then you can change the source of supply during the simulation.  Purchasing info record A purchasing info record is a one-to-one material-to-supplier relationship that is needed for the pMRP process so that the system can assign at least one source of supply to each material that is procured.  Planned independent requirements PIRs for the relevant materials must be maintained. All of this data is also used by MRP for planning materials. Before you start to use pMRP, all of the relevant master data must be available. As one of the main objectives behind pMRP is to allow the user to check whether there is enough capacity to produce the forecasted quantities, it’s very important to correctly set up the routing and the work center with the standard values and the proper formu- las. From a transactional data perspective, the main input for pMRP is a demand plan, which is represented by PIRs (Transaction MD61). The planning strategy used isn’t rele- vant because it supports any requirement type, and you can use an active or an inactive PIR version. When choosing an inactive version, the capacity planner will need to select the version number during simulation creation. 15.2 Setup The first step in the pMRP process is to create a pMRP simulation, wherein you as a planner can choose to restrict a set of master data for simulation purposes. When you create a simulation, you can select which top-level materials, components, or work cen- ters will be considered for pMRP. In pMRP, the planning will happen during the simula- tion creation itself. With pMRP, you will be able to process the simulation immediately after the creation is finished and will not have to wait for a planning run. The pMRP 15 Predictive Material and Resource Planning 840 process uses simplified planning logic, in which all materials use a deterministic MRP and a lot-for-lot procedure. Before creating the simulation, you must ensure that the relevant master data has been created. You must also have created the PIRs, since they will be the main input into the pMRP simulation. The system will plan the selected materials and determine the work center capacity requirements based on those PIRs. A word of caution here: when a simulation is created, master data will be copied into it, so subsequent changes to master data may not be considered. Creating a pMRP simulation is basically a background job that you can schedule through the Schedule pMRP Simulation Creation app. You can also use this application to manage background jobs that are already finished, scheduled, or in process. As shown in Figure 15.2, an icon in the Log column will show the status of the finished background executions, and another icon appears in the Results column. Choosing the icon in the Log column will show the details of success, warning, or error messages that may have been triggered during each step of simulation creation. You can create, copy, and delete a simulation creation (although deletion is only possi- ble for scheduled jobs). To create a new application job, choose Create on the screen shown in Figure 15.2, which will bring up the screen shown in Figure 15.3. Figure 15.2 Application Jobs On the screen shown in Figure 15.3. you can use the dropdown list in the Job Template field to choose from the following three job templates, which have different selection criteria:  Creation of pMRP Data via Top-Level Materials In this template, object selection is based on the material master, so the selection cri- teria will be focused on material master information, such as material number, MRP controller, and low-level code. The system will look for PIRs for the relevant materi- als and run simplified MRP to determine the required quantity for each level and the capacity allocated in the work center. © 841 15.2 Setup  Creation of pMRP Data via Components Selecting this template will enable you to select components as inputs for creating the simulation. In this case, pMRP will use the BOM to find relevant upper-level materials and look for demands for these materials.  Creation of pMRP Data via Work Center In this template, object selection is based on the work center, so the selection criteria will be focused on the work center. The system will look for capacity requirements in the selected work centers and then identify the top-level materials and the respec- tive PIRs. For this example, you choose the first option from the dropdown list in Figure 15.3 1 and then click the Step 2 button. Figure 15.3 Scheduling pMRP Then, in the Scheduling Options section 2, you define whether the job will be executed immediately or scheduled to run on a future date. The creation of the pMRP simulation will be executed only once; therefore, it should not be executed as a periodic job, and the Recurrence Pattern value will be set to Single-Run by default. Then, click the Step 3 but- ton on the screen shown in Figure 15.3 to make the screen shown in Figure 15.4 appear. In the Parameter Section of the screen shown in Figure 15.4, fill in the ID for Reference Plan and Simulation ID fields, which are used to identify the simulation. You should use unique values; the reference ID and simulation ID cannot be the same. The ID for the 15 Predictive Material and Resource Planning 842 reference plan will represent the set of master data selected according to the selection criteria, and you can add new simulations later under the same reference ID. Then, in the Parameter Section, select the Bucket Category (daily, weekly, or monthly buckets) and the start and end date for the simulation. Figure 15.4 Parameters Selection in pMRP Scheduling, Part 1 In the Limitations section, there are more fields you can use to restrict the selection. You can use these fields to ensure that pMRP will be executed only for materials with a specific BOM, routing, or material status, or for a BOM or task list usage. Then, scroll down the screen shown in Figure 15.4 until the screen shown in Figure 15.5 appears. The Object Selection section of the screen shown in Figure 15.5 contains the fields that you will use to select materials or work centers. Depending on the job template you’ve selected, you’ll see material-related fields (such as the Material, Plant, MRP Controller, Material Type, and Low-Level Code) or work center-related fields (such as Work Center, Work Center Category, and Person Responsible) here. You can also define whether stock transfers will be considered in the scenario and which plants and which work centers from those supplying plants should be considered in the simulation. Finally, in the Document Data section, you choose whether the opening stock will be zero, whether it will be the safety stock or the actual material stock at the plant, whether an inactive PIR version will be considered instead of the active version, and whether the sim- ple discontinuation will be considered. You define all of these settings in the reference plan while creating the simulation. You cannot change them later, when you’re adding new simulations to the same ref- erence plan. Once you click the Schedule button, the background job to create the new simulation will be scheduled. Depending on the number of materials you select for the simulation, the job may take some time because it executes an actual planning © 843 15.2 Setup run. We highly recommend that you first check the completeness and correctness of the data you’ve maintained by choosing Check; the message that will appear at the bottom of the screen will confirm whether the application job can be scheduled. Figure 15.5 Parameters Selection in pMRP Scheduling, Part 2 Figure 15.6 shows the details of the simulation creation logs, including the success and error messages that have been triggered. When you choose the icon in the Results col- umn shown previously in Figure 15.2, the screen will jump into the spool, which dis- plays a list of the materials and work centers selected for the simulation. Figure 15.6 Application Log After you create the pMRP simulation, you will be able to process the simulation in the Process pMRP Simulations app, as discussed in the next section. 15 Predictive Material and Resource Planning 844
sections.he:
• **BOM:** ‏BOM תקף עם BOM usage = 1—Production לחומר בסימולציה.
• **Work center:** עם לפחות קיבולת אחת רלוונטית ל-finite scheduling.
• **Routing:** תקף, עם פעולת ה-bottleneck רלוונטית לתכנון קיבולת.
• **Production version:** לפחות אחת תקפה המתייחסת ל-BOM ול-routing. אם יש יותר מאחת, ניתן לשנות מקור אספקה בסימולציה.
• **Purchasing info record:** יחס 1:1 חומר-ספק — נדרש כך שהמערכת תקצה מקור אספקה לכל חומר נרכש.
• **PIRs:** חובה לתחזק לחומרים הרלוונטיים.
כל הנתונים משמשים גם את MRP. לפני pMRP, כל נתוני האב חייבים להיות זמינים. מאחר שמטרה עיקרית היא לבדוק אם יש קיבולת לייצור הכמויות החזויות, חשוב להגדיר נכון את ה-routing וה-work center עם ערכי התקן והנוסחאות.
הקלט העיקרי הוא demand plan — ‏PIRs (Transaction MD61). האסטרטגיה אינה רלוונטית (תומך בכל סוג דרישה), וניתן גרסת PIR פעילה או לא-פעילה. בלא-פעילה, מתכנן הקיבולת בוחר את מספר הגרסה ביצירת הסימולציה.

הצעד הראשון — יצירת סימולציית pMRP, בה ניתן להגביל קבוצת נתוני אב. בוחרים אילו top-level materials, רכיבים, או work centers ייכללו. התכנון מתרחש בעת היצירה עצמה — ניתן לעבד מיד ללא המתנה לריצה. ‏pMRP משתמש בלוגיקה מפושטת — כל החומרים ב-MRP דטרמיניסטי ו-lot-for-lot.
לפני היצירה, ודאו שנתוני האב וה-PIRs נוצרו (הקלט העיקרי). המערכת תתכנן את החומרים ותקבע דרישות קיבולת לפי ה-PIRs.
**אזהרה:** ביצירת סימולציה, נתוני האב מועתקים אליה — שינויים מאוחרים עשויים לא להישקל.
יצירת סימולציה היא job רקע דרך Schedule pMRP Simulation Creation. ניתן גם לנהל jobs (שהושלמו/מתוזמנים/בעיבוד). דגל בטור Log מציג סטטוס, ובטור Results סמל נוסף (Figure 15.2). ניתן ליצור/להעתיק/למחוק (מחיקה רק ל-jobs מתוזמנים). בחרו Create (Figure 15.3).
ב-Job Template, שלוש תבניות:
• **Creation of pMRP Data via Top-Level Materials:** בחירה לפי אב החומר (מספר, ‏MRP controller, ‏low-level code). המערכת מחפשת PIRs, מריצה MRP מפושט, וקובעת כמות וקיבולת.
• **Creation of pMRP Data via Components:** בחירת רכיבים כקלט; ‏pMRP משתמש ב-BOM למציאת חומרי-על ודרישות.
• **Creation of pMRP Data via Work Center:** בחירה לפי work center; המערכת מחפשת דרישות קיבולת ומזהה top-level materials ו-PIRs.
בדוגמה, האפשרות הראשונה (Figure 15.3), ‏Step 2. ב-Scheduling Options, מיד או בעתיד. היצירה פעם אחת — ‏Recurrence Pattern = Single-Run. ‏Step 3 (Figure 15.4).
ב-Parameter Section, מלאו ID for Reference Plan ו-Simulation ID (ייחודיים; לא זהים). ה-reference מייצג את קבוצת נתוני האב; ניתן להוסיף סימולציות תחת אותו reference ID. בחרו Bucket Category (יומי/שבועי/חודשי) ותאריכי התחלה וסיום.
ב-Limitations, הגבלות (BOM, ‏routing, ‏material status, ‏usage). גללו (Figure 15.5).
ב-Object Selection, שדות לבחירת חומרים/work centers (לפי התבנית). ניתן להגדיר אם stock transfers נשקלים ואילו מפעלים/work centers. ב-Document Data, בחרו אם המלאי הפתיחתי יהיה אפס/safety stock/בפועל, אם גרסת PIR לא-פעילה תישקל, ואם discontinuation פשוט.
כל ההגדרות ב-reference plan ביצירה — לא ניתן לשנותן בהוספת סימולציות. ב-Schedule, ה-job מתוזמן (עשוי לקחת זמן — ריצת תכנון בפועל). מומלץ Check תחילה.
Figure 15.6 — יומני היצירה (הצלחה ושגיאות). בסמל Results (Figure 15.2), קפיצה ל-spool עם רשימת החומרים וה-work centers. לאחר היצירה, עבדו ב-Process pMRP Simulations.

sections.title: Managing pMRP
sections.en: 15.3 Managing pMRP In the Process pMRP Simulations app, you as a planner will actually work with the sim- ulation, analyze the planning results, identify and resolve capacity issues, and validate the forecast you’ve created. Once the simulation is processed, you can release the results to operational planning in the form of PIRs. Then, the forecast can become rele- vant to MRP. When you open this app, it will display a list of all the created simulations, including the total number of capacity issues, the delivery performance, and the simulation sta- tus. These appear in separate columns. The number of capacity issues represents the total number of buckets in which a capacity issue was identified, and the delivery per- formance represents the percentage of the originally planned forecast that can be ful- filled. For example, if a capacity issue is found and the forecast quantity was reduced to resolve the issue, then the delivery performance will be adjusted accordingly. The Simulation Status column is related to the results of the simulation creation; if the status is Created with Warnings or Fatal Errors, you can refer to the simulation creation logs shown in Figure 15.7. Figure 15.7 Processing pMRP Simulations In this application, you also have the option to copy, rename, or delete an existing sim- ulation or override errors. When you copy a simulation, it will be linked to the same ref- erence data as the original simulation. Also, you can choose whether to copy data from the simulation or from the reference data, as shown in Figure 15.8. If you choose to copy from the simulation, then changes already made to the simulation will also be copied; if you choose to copy from the reference data, changes made to the simulation will not be considered and the original forecast quantities from the reference data will be cop- ied. You can also add a percentage for the Overload Tolerance value so that pMRP will not consider a work center overload until reaching the tolerance. © 845 15.3 Managing pMRP When you choose one of the simulations, the Demand Plan Simulation screen will appear (see Figure 15.9). This screen shows the lines with the materials selected for the simulation, and each column represents the forecast quantity for a specific bucket. Some cells are highlighted in red because there is an issue with a capacity overload in the work center: the forecasted quantities will require more time to be produced than is available with the current shift schedules in the work centers. The capacity issue may be related to either top-level materials or a semifinished product in the BOM’s lower levels. Figure 15.8 Copying pMRP Simulation Figure 15.9 Demand Plan Simulation The Demand Plan Simulation screen shows the number of capacity issues, but there’s no issue with delivery performance. The number of capacity issues will not necessarily match the number of highlighted cells; two or more cells may be highlighted due to the same capacity issue in a specific work center. In this example, the delivery performance is still 100% because the originally forecasted quantities have not yet been changed, but this number may change when a supply chain planner tries to resolve the capacity issues caused by the forecasted quantities. We’ll cover that scenario later in this chap- ter. On this screen, you choose from the following options in the Quantities Displayed dropdown list: 15 Predictive Material and Resource Planning 846  Simulation Only This column shows the forecast quantities related to the simulation.  Reference/Simulation Two columns will appear: the original quantity from the reference and the simula- tion quantities. With this option, you can compare the changes made to the simula- tion with the original quantities to form a better estimation of the impact of the changes over the originally forecasted quantity.  Delta of the Reference and Simulation This column only shows the difference between the reference and the simulation. This view also helps you estimate the impacts of the changes you’ve made in the simulation. If you choose Capacity Plan Simulation from the Simulation Views dropdown list located in the top right-hand corner of Figure 15.9, a different screen will appear. It focuses on work center capacity, as shown in Figure 15.10. The upper part of the screen shows a list of the work centers selected for this simulation, with the total number of hours allocated and the remaining capacity of the work centers for every month. In the lower part of the screen, a chart shows a graphical overview of the work centers’ possi- ble load and the overload. In the chart bars, the green area represents the feasible load (the capacity requirements that can be fulfilled with the current work center capacity), and the red area represents the capacity overload that is causing the issue. Figure 15.10 Capacity Plan Simulation In the capacity plan simulation, two buttons correspond to the two alternatives for dealing with the capacity issues:  Disregard Capacity Issues The pMRP process will simply ignore all the existing capacity issues for the selected work center. The total number of capacity issues will be reduced, and the cells will no longer be highlighted in red. © 847 15.3 Managing pMRP  Change Available Capacity You can change the work center’s available capacity to allow for a capacity overload. When you choose this option, a popup will appear (see Figure 15.11), wherein you can choose months and the percentage of overload allowed. Months with a capacity issue will be highlighted in red, and the system will also propose a capacity utiliza- tion that can resolve the capacity issue for each month. Be sure to select one or more relevant months from the Months to Show dropdown so that the system brings up the option to make changes to the existing capacities. Figure 15.11 Changing Available Capacity On both the Capacity Plan Simulation screen and the Demand Plan Simulation screen, if you choose the Inspector view, the system will display a side panel with additional information about the selected object (see Figure 15.12). When you’re using the Inspec- tor on the Capacity Plan Simulation screen, the inspected objects will be the work cen- ter and the capacity allocated for the selected month, and the Inspector will also show the top-level materials related to the capacity allocated in the work center. Figure 15.12 Inspector Panel 15 Predictive Material and Resource Planning 848 If you use the Inspector tool from the Demand Plan Simulation screen, then the inspected objects will be the material and the quantity forecasted for the selected month. The tool will also display the capacity issues related to the forecast created for this specific top-level material, even if they’re caused by a material in the lower BOM levels. Also, when you’re using the Inspector from the Demand Plan Simulation screen, a link will appear that, when clicked, will bring up the multilevel material simulation for the selected demand. Figure 15.12 shows the Inspector view for a demand plan simulation. It includes links to the Multi-Level Material Simulation and the capacity plan simulation for the work cen- ters with capacity issues. (The latter is not shown, but scrolling down will reveal it). The screen in Figure 15.13 will appear when you select the Simulation Components option from the Simulation Views dropdown list in Figure 15.12. This view is a summary of various components and their availability in the chosen time bucket. (Here, it’s the monthly time bucket.) Figure 15.13 Simulation Components If you click the Multi-Level Material Simulation link, the system will bring up a screen with a complete BOM for a specific bucket, including the details of the required and missing quantities for each material in each BOM level (see Figure 15.14). There may be a number of issues and a number of sources of supply available for each material; therefore, it’s possible to identify on exactly which BOM level there is a capacity issue. Figure 15.14 shows the details of the multilevel material simulation, and it indicates that several materials have capacity issues. In the multilevel material simulation, it’s also possible to resolve the capacity issues for top-level and lower-level materials. For materials with several sources of supply (and thus with several valid production versions), you can select the Change Source of © 849 15.3 Managing pMRP Supply option and then select a different production version. When you choose this option, a popup appears (see Figure 15.15) in which you can distribute the forecasted quantity among the different production versions that are available for the selected material. Here, you’ll see an overview of the available capacity for each source of supply and a proposed distribution of the forecast quantity among the different production versions. Also, you can manually define the quantity distribution or select the Adopt Proposal option (see Figure 15.15) to automatically adopt the proposed distribution. Figure 15.14 Multilevel Material Simulation Figure 15.15 Changing Source of Supply Figure 15.16 shows that the demand for the month of January 2025 is being shifted to Feb- ruary 2025 (preproduction) to balance the capacity overload at the given work center. 15 Predictive Material and Resource Planning 850 Figure 15.16 Shifting Top-Level Demand The Pull In Quantity option shown in Figure 15.14 will enable you as a capacity and materials planner to either preproduce an in-house-produced material or request early procurement of an externally procured material (see Figure 15.17). Figure 15.17 Preproduction or Early Procurement of Components If there are still any unresolved issues that need attention or the action of a capacity planner, then you can evaluate these issues in the Issue List (see Figure 15.18). Here, you can choose to disregard the capacity overload issues you face. © 851 15.3 Managing pMRP Figure 15.18 Issue List Figure 15.19 is the Demand Plan Simulation screen, which shows that reducing the orig- inal PIRs leads to poorer delivery performance. For this example, previously, delivery performance was 100%, but after a reduction of the PIRs for a few months, delivery per- formance has correspondingly decreased to 86%. The right-hand side of the screen shows the complete log or history of all the changes made to this pMRP plan. Figure 15.19 Delivery Performance Impacted Tips and Tricks If you choose one of the many KPIs displayed at the header level in Figure 15.19, a popup will appear and show you more details about the issues facing the KPI. From this popup, you as a planner can navigate to the detailed list, which is basically an issue list, to better understand and address the issues in hand. 15 Predictive Material and Resource Planning 852 On any of the main screens of the Process pMRP Simulations app, the Simulation Sum- mary button is available, and clicking it gives you an overview of all the changes made while you’ve been processing the simulation. The following change categories will be shown:  Changes in Demand  Changes in Capacity  Preproduction or Early Procurement  Changes in Source of Supply  Unresolved Issues  Disregarded Capacity Issues Figure 15.20 shows the Simulation Summary screen, which has tabs for the different change categories and the total number in each category. You can also export this table to a spreadsheet so that you can further discuss and validate the forecast changes. Figure 15.20 Simulation Summary
sections.he:
ב-Process pMRP Simulations עובדים עם הסימולציה — מנתחים, מזהים ופותרים בעיות קיבולת, ומאמתים את החיזוי. בסיום, משחררים ל-תכנון תפעולי כ-PIRs.
האפליקציה מציגה את הסימולציות, סך בעיות הקיבולת, ביצועי האספקה (delivery performance), והסטטוס. מספר בעיות הקיבולת = ה-buckets שבהם זוהתה בעיה; ביצועי האספקה = אחוז החיזוי המקורי שניתן למילוי. אם בעיה נפתרה בהפחתת חיזוי, הביצועים מתעדכנים.
טור Simulation Status קשור לתוצאות היצירה; אם Created with Warnings או Fatal Errors, ראו את היומנים (Figure 15.7).
ניתן להעתיק/לשנות-שם/למחוק או לדרוס שגיאות. בהעתקה, מקושר לאותו reference data. בוחרים אם להעתיק מהסימולציה או מה-reference (Figure 15.8) — מהסימולציה (כולל שינויים) או מה-reference (כמויות מקוריות). ניתן Overload Tolerance — ‏pMRP לא ישקול עומס-יתר עד הסבילות.
בבחירת סימולציה, מסך Demand Plan Simulation (Figure 15.9). שורות = חומרים, עמודות = כמות חיזוי ל-bucket. תאים אדומים = עומס-יתר ב-work center (הכמויות דורשות יותר זמן מהזמין). הבעיה יכולה להיות בחומר top-level או בחצי-גמור ברמות נמוכות.
מספר בעיות הקיבולת לא בהכרח תואם למספר התאים המסומנים (שניים+ מאותה בעיה). בדוגמה, הביצועים עדיין 100% (הכמויות לא שונו), אך עשוי להשתנות בניסיון לפתור.
רשימת Quantities Displayed:
• **Simulation Only:** כמויות הסימולציה.
• **Reference/Simulation:** שתי עמודות (מקורי מול סימולציה) — להשוואת ההשפעה.
• **Delta of the Reference and Simulation:** רק ההפרש.
ברשימת Simulation Views, בחירת Capacity Plan Simulation (Figure 15.10) — ממוקד בקיבולת. למעלה — work centers עם שעות מוקצות וקיבולת נותרת לכל חודש. למטה — תרשים: ירוק = עומס בר-מימוש, אדום = עומס-יתר.
שני כפתורים לטיפול:
• **Disregard Capacity Issues:** התעלמות מכל הבעיות ל-work center — המספר יורד והתאים מפסיקים להיות אדומים.
• **Change Available Capacity:** שינוי הקיבולת הזמינה לאפשר עומס-יתר (Figure 15.11) — בחרו חודשים ואחוז. חודשים עם בעיה מסומנים אדום, והמערכת מציעה ניצול לפתרון.
ב-Inspector (Figure 15.12), פאנל צד עם מידע נוסף. ב-Capacity Plan Simulation — ה-work center והקיבולת לחודש, ו-top-level materials. ב-Demand Plan Simulation — החומר והכמות החזויה, ובעיות הקיבולת (גם מרמות נמוכות), וקישור ל-multilevel material simulation.
בחירת Simulation Components (Figure 15.13) — סיכום רכיבים וזמינותם ב-bucket.
בקישור Multi-Level Material Simulation (Figure 15.14) — BOM מלא ל-bucket, עם כמויות נדרשות וחסרות בכל רמה. ניתן לזהות באיזו רמה הבעיה.
במולטי-לבל ניתן גם לפתור בעיות. לחומרים עם מספר מקורות (גרסאות), בחרו Change Source of Supply ובחרו גרסה (Figure 15.15) — חלקו את החיזוי בין הגרסאות (ידנית או Adopt Proposal).
Figure 15.16 — הביקוש לינואר 2025 מוזז לפברואר 2025 (preproduction) לאיזון העומס.
‏Pull In Quantity (Figure 15.14) — ייצור-מוקדם של חומר פנימי או רכש מוקדם של חיצוני (Figure 15.17).
בעיות לא-פתורות — ב-Issue List (Figure 15.18); ניתן להתעלם.
Figure 15.19 — הפחתת ה-PIRs המקוריים מורידה את הביצועים (מ-100% ל-86%). בימין — יומן השינויים.
**Tips and Tricks:** בחירת KPI בכותרת (Figure 15.19) מציגה חלון עם פרטים; ניתן לנווט לרשימת הבעיות.
כפתור Simulation Summary — סקירת כל השינויים, בקטגוריות:
• Changes in Demand
• Changes in Capacity
• Preproduction or Early Procurement
• Changes in Source of Supply
• Unresolved Issues
• Disregarded Capacity Issues
(Figure 15.20 — לשוניות לקטגוריות; ניתן לייצא ל-spreadsheet.)

sections.title: Releasing Results to Operative Material Requirements Planning
sections.en: 15.4 Releasing Results to Operative Material Requirements Planning Once the simulation process is complete and you’ve identified and resolved all of the capacity issues, or if you as a capacity planner decide to disregard them or compromise on delivery performance, then you can release the pMRP simulation. You accomplish this by choosing the Release button on the initial screen of the Process pMRP Simula- tions app. This brings up a popup (see Figure 15.21) in which you can confirm whether the simulation can be released, and the forecast will be transferred to the top-level materials in an inactive version 01, even if you created the simulation with active PIRs as references. The option to transfer PIRs into an active version also exists in the same © 853 15.4 Releasing Results to Operative Material Requirements Planning popup (see Version Active: Yes). Also, as mentioned at the beginning of this chapter, in the latest version of SAP S/4HANA, DDMRP can also consider PIRs for the buffer calcu- lation. This means that the pMRP simulation results will be an input for DDMRP. When the simulation is released, if there are DDMRP materials in the BOM’s lower levels, then PIRs will be created for DDMRP materials, even if there was no PIR for those materials before the simulation creation. Therefore, the buffer calculation will take into consider- ation any demand variability that can be anticipated by the forecast. Furthermore, you can copy the inactive PIRs created by DDMRP to the active version in Transaction MD70. Alternatively, you can simply check the Active flag in Transaction MD62 to activate PIRs. When you release a simulation, the Show Log option (not shown) will provide a complete log of the PIRs that are transferred. If you need to, you can check the Subassembly Components box to bring up the option to transfer the sub- components of the main assembly in the chosen version (see Requirements Version* in Figure 15.21). Furthermore, the pMRP tool in SAP S/4HANA 2023 offers even more options for the system to consider materials that are managed via Kanban (discussed in Chapter 9) and even non-MRP materials. Figure 15.21 Releasing pMRP Simulation Figure 15.22 shows the updated status of the pMRP simulation that has been processed, and the Simulation Status denotes that it is Released. 15 Predictive Material and Resource Planning 854 Figure 15.22 Processed Simulation Released to Operative MRP You access the screen shown in Figure 15.23 via Transaction MD62. It shows that Mate- rial 2269 in Plant 1710 now has updated PIRs transferred through pMRP simulation. Because this PIR is now in operative planning, it’s ready for the MRP run. Figure 15.23 Updated Planned Independent Requirements Next, refer to Figure 15.21 again. If you checked the Capacity Changes Proposals box during pMRP release, then the system will be able to adopt the capacity changes you made during the simulation and also update the work center capacity using the Mass Maintenance of the Work Center Capacities app (see Figure 15.24). When you open this app, you can select the pMRP Change Proposal flag to see a list of all the changes pro- posed by pMRP simulations. When you select one of the lines, you’ll be able to see the details of the capacity change proposed by the pMRP simulation, including the month and the proposed capacity utiliztion. Or, you can simply reject the proposal if it’s not possible to implement it. Figure 15.24 Changes to pMRP in the Mass Maintenance of Work Center Capacities App © 855
sections.he:
בסיום העיבוד ופתרון/התעלמות מהבעיות, ניתן לשחרר את הסימולציה ב-Release (מסך Process pMRP Simulations). בחלון (Figure 15.21) מאשרים, והחיזוי מועבר ל-top-level materials בגרסה לא-פעילה 01 (גם אם נוצר עם PIRs פעילים). קיימת אפשרות העברה לגרסה פעילה (Version Active: Yes). כפי שצוין, ‏DDMRP יכול לשקול PIRs לחישוב buffer — לכן תוצאות ה-pMRP יהיו קלט ל-DDMRP. אם יש חומרי DDMRP ברמות נמוכות, ייווצרו להם PIRs (גם אם לא היו לפני). כך חישוב ה-buffer ישקול שונות ביקוש צפויה.
ניתן להעתיק את ה-PIRs הלא-פעילים שנוצרו לגרסה פעילה ב-Transaction MD70, או לסמן Active ב-Transaction MD62. ב-Show Log — יומן ה-PIRs שהועברו. סמנו Subassembly Components להעברת תת-רכיבים (Requirements Version, ‏Figure 15.21). ‏pMRP ב-S/4HANA 2023 מציע גם שקילת חומרי Kanban (פרק 9) וחומרים שאינם MRP.
Figure 15.22 — הסטטוס Released. ‏Figure 15.23 (Transaction MD62) — חומר 2269/מפעל 1710 עם PIRs מעודכנים מהסימולציה, מוכן לריצת MRP.
אם סומן Capacity Changes Proposals בשחרור (Figure 15.21), המערכת תאמץ את שינויי הקיבולת ותעדכן את הקיבולת באפליקציית Mass Maintenance of the Work Center Capacities (Figure 15.24). סמנו pMRP Change Proposal לרשימת ההצעות; בבחירת שורה — פרטי השינוי (חודש וניצול מוצע). ניתן גם לדחות.

sections.title: Using Flexible Constraints
sections.en: 15.5 Using Flexible Constraints 15.5 Using Flexible Constraints The pMRP functionality allows you as a planner to define flexible constraints for prod- ucts. For example, you can define that a maximum quantity of a certain material can be produced or purchased in any given time period (week or month). If this quantity is exceeded, pMRP will generate an alert when processing the pMRP simulation. You can also define flexible constraints for a single material or multiple materials, and you can used them for materials produced in house, externally procured materials, or stock transfer materials. The available periodicities are weeks and months. To define a flexible constraint, you use the Define Flexible Constraints app (see Figure 15.25 1). In this example, we use the same material, 2269, in plant 1710, and we have defined a constraint that whenever the production quantity is more than 75 pieces (PC) during the period from August 2024 to February 2025, then the system should consider this constraint while processing pMRP. When you’ve scheduled the pMRP and you pro- ceed to process it, the system will show the Violated Constraints (see Figure 15.25 2). Figure 15.25 Flexible Constraint 15 Predictive Material and Resource Planning 856 Since pMRP is an interactive tool, any changes made during processing will immediately be reflected. For example, in 2, if you reduce the quantity of Material 2269 below 75 PC, then the system will accordingly update (reduce) the status of the violated constraints. Clicking on the Violated Constraints field will bring up detailed information on all the constraints that have been violated.
sections.he:
pMRP מאפשר להגדיר flexible constraints למוצרים. למשל, כמות מקסימלית לייצור/רכש בתקופה (שבוע/חודש); בחריגה, ‏pMRP מתריע. ניתן לחומר בודד או מרובים, לפנימי/חיצוני/stock transfer. המחזוריות — שבועות וחודשים.
להגדרה: Define Flexible Constraints (Figure 15.25). בדוגמה, חומר 2269/מפעל 1710, אילוץ שבכל ייצור מעל 75 PC בתקופה אוגוסט 2024–פברואר 2025 המערכת תשקול. בעיבוד, מוצגים Violated Constraints (Figure 15.25).
מאחר ש-pMRP אינטראקטיבי, שינויים משתקפים מיד. למשל, הפחתת 2269 מתחת ל-75 PC תעדכן (תפחית) את האילוצים שהופרו. לחיצה על Violated Constraints — מידע מפורט.

sections.title: Summary
sections.en: 15.6 Summary The pMRP functionality is the latest innovation in SAP S/4HANA, and it offers simula- tion capabilities that can be used by production and capacity planners to make fore- casting from a work center capacity point of view both practical and achievable. With pMRP, a supply chain planner can change forecasted quantities and evaluate the results, test different sources of supply for different products, and consider the prepro- duction of certain critical products to avoid a capacity overload in a specific month. The pMRP functionality is still in the development phase, and more innovations are expected to be delivered in future releases of SAP S/4HANA. The next chapter covers capacity requirements planning, which includes capacity eval- uation and capacity leveling.
sections.he: pMRP הוא החידוש האחרון ב-S/4HANA, ומציע יכולות סימולציה למתכנני ייצור וקיבולת — להפוך את החיזוי, מנקודת מבט קיבולת ה-work center, למעשי ובר-השגה. עם pMRP, מתכנן יכול לשנות כמויות חזויות ולהעריך תוצאות, לבחון מקורות אספקה שונים, ולשקול ייצור-מוקדם של מוצרים קריטיים למניעת עומס-יתר בחודש מסוים. ‏pMRP עדיין בפיתוח — חידושים נוספים צפויים בגרסאות עתידיות. הפרק הבא — capacity requirements planning (הערכת קיבולת ואיזון קיבולת).
